children.text: Chapter 1
atha niṣekādisaṃskārānvyākhyāsyāmaḥ
children.translated_text: Now we shall explain the <s>saṃskāras</s> (sacraments) beginning with <s>niṣeka</s> (impregnation).

children.text: ṛtusaṃgamanagarbhādhānapuṃsavanasīmantaviṣṇubalijātakarmotthānanāmakaraṇānnaprāśanapravāsāgamanapiṇḍavardhanattau?akopanayanapārāyaṇavratabandhavisargopākarmasamāvartanapāṇigrahaṇānīty aṣṭādaśa saṃskārāḥ śārīrāḥ yajñāśca dvāviṃśat brahmayajño devayajñaḥ pitṛyajño bhūtayajño manuṣyayajñaśceti pañcānāmaharaharanuṣṭhānaṃ sthālīpāka āgrayaṇamaṣṭakā piṇḍapitṛyajño māsiśrāddhaṃ caitryāśvayujīti sapta pākayajñāḥ agnyādheyamagnihotraṃ darśapūrṇamāsāvāgrayaṇeṣṭiścāturmāsyo nirūḍhapaśubandhaḥ sautrāmaṇīti sapta haviryajñāḥ agniṣṭomo 'tyagniṣṭoma ukthyaḥ ṣoḍaśī vājapeyo 'tirātro 'ptoryāma iti sapta somayajñā ityete catvāriṃśadbhavanti niṣekādā jātakātsaṃskṛtāyāṃ brāhmaṇyāṃ brāhmaṇājjātamātraḥ putramātra upanītaḥ sāvitryadhyayanādbrāhmaṇo vedamadhītya śārīrair ā pāṇigrahaṇātsaṃskṛtaḥ pākayajñairapi yajan śrotriyaḥ svādhyāyapara āhitāgnirhaviryajñair apyanūttānaḥ somayajñairapi bhrūṇaḥ saṃskārairetairupeto niyamayamābhyāmṛṣikalpaḥ sāṅgacaturvedatapoyogādṛṣiḥ nārāyaṇaparāyaṇo nirdvaṃdvo muniriti saṃskāraviśeṣāt pūrvātpūrvātparovarīvāniti vijñāyate ||
children.translated_text: Seasonal intercourse, the rite of placing the embryo, the rite for producing a male child, parting the pregnant woman's hair, the offering to <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the birth rite, the rite of rising, name-giving, the first feeding of solid food, departure and return from travel, the rite for increasing the bodily frame, the [corruptly transmitted, apparently tonsure] rite, initiation, recitation, release from the binding vow, commencement of Vedic study, return home after study, and taking a wife—these are the eighteen bodily <s>saṃskāras</s>. The sacrifices are twenty-two. The <s>Brahmayajña</s>, sacrifice to the gods, sacrifice to the ancestors, sacrifice to beings, and sacrifice to human guests—these five are to be performed every day. The <s>sthālīpāka</s> (cooked-pot offering), first-fruits offering, <s>aṣṭakā</s>, offering of rice balls to the ancestors, monthly ancestral rite, the <s>Caitrī</s>, and the <s>Āśvayujī</s> are the seven cooked-food sacrifices. Establishing the sacred fire, the <s>Agnihotra</s>, the new- and full-moon sacrifices, the first-fruits oblation, the four-monthly sacrifices, the sacrifice of a tethered animal, and the <s>Sautrāmaṇī</s> are the seven oblation sacrifices. The <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>, <s>Atyagniṣṭoma</s>, <s>Ukthya</s>, <s>Ṣoḍaśin</s>, <s>Vājapeya</s>, <s>Atirātra</s>, and <s>Aptoryāma</s> are the seven Soma sacrifices. These amount to forty. From impregnation through birth, a male merely born of a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> father to a consecrated <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> woman is merely a son. Once initiated, he becomes a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> through study of the <s>Sāvitrī</s>. Having studied the Veda, having been consecrated by the bodily rites through marriage, and also performing the cooked-food sacrifices, he is a <s>śrotriya</s> (Veda-learned man). Devoted to private recitation, having established his sacred fires, and also performing the oblation sacrifices, he is an <s>anūttāna</s> [a learned ritual rank; reading uncertain]. By also performing the Soma sacrifices he is a <s>bhrūṇa</s> [a further ritual rank]. Endowed with these sacraments and with restraint and observances, he is like a seer; through asceticism and yoga together with the four Vedas and their ancillary sciences, he becomes a seer; devoted to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> and free from the pairs of opposites, he is a sage. Thus it is understood that, by distinction of sacraments, each succeeding rank is more eminent than the one before it.

children.text: atha cāturāśramiṇāṃ svānavidhirabhiṣekadivyavāyavyāgneyagurvanujñā iti pañcadhā bhavati nadītaṭākakūpānāmalābhe pūrvasyottaramupatiṣṭhate prāṅmukha udaṅmukho vākramya jalasthaleṣvāsīnaḥ pāṇipādāv ā maṇibandhajānuto dakṣiṇādi pratyekaṃ prakṣālyākenāvastrāvamavicchinnam adrutam aśabdam abahirjānuhṛdayaṃgamam udakaṃ gokarṇavatpāṇiṃ kṛtvā brāhmeṇa tīrthena trirācamya dviraṅguṣṭhamūlenāsyaṃ parimārṣṭyaṅguṣṭhasyāgniḥ pradeśinyā vāyurmadhyamasya prajāpatiranāmikāyāḥ sūryaḥ kaniṣṭhikasyendra ityadhidevatā bhavantyaṅguṣṭhamadhyamābhyāṃ sarvatīrthairvā mukhaṃ mārṣṭyaṅguṣṭhānāmikābhyāṃ cakṣuṣī aṅguṣṭhapradeśinībhyāṃ nāsikāmaṅguṣṭhakaniṣṭhikābhyāṃ śrotre bhujau tābhyāmaṅguṣṭhena vā hṛdayamaṅgulibhirnābhiṃ cāṅguṣṭhena pratyaṅgamapaśca spṛṣṭvā jaṅghayorvāme pāṇāvapyabhyukṣya sarvābhirmūrdhānaṃ spṛśatīndro 'ham ubhayābhyām iti karāvāpaḥ pādāvasminkula iti pādau ca tathā prakṣālyāpaḥ punantviti punastathācāmati ṛgvedaḥ prīṇātu yajurvedaḥ prīṇātu sāmavedaḥ prīṇātviti trir apaḥ pītvātharvavedaḥ prīṇātvitihāsavedaḥ prīṇātu candramāḥ prīṇātviti tridhā mukhaṃ mārṣṭi maheśvaraḥ prīṇātviti mūrdhānamādityaḥ prīṇātu somaḥ prīṇātviti cakṣuṣī diśaḥ prīṇantviti śrotre vāyuḥ prīṇātviti nāsikāmindraḥ prīṇātviti bhujau viṣṇuḥ prīṇātviti hṛdayamagniḥ prīṇātviti nābhiṃ spṛśatītyeke ||
children.translated_text: Now the rule for bathing for members of the four orders of life is of five kinds: bathing by pouring water over oneself, divine bathing, airy bathing, fiery bathing, and bathing with the teacher's permission. If a river, pond, or well is unavailable, one resorts to each following means in place of the preceding one. Facing east or north, having entered and seated himself at a place with water, he washes his hands and feet—as far as the wrists and knees respectively—beginning with the right. Taking a single continuous draught of water, unhurried, noiseless, not passing outside the knees, and sufficient to reach the heart, he shapes his hand like a cow's ear and sips three times from the <s>brāhma tīrtha</s> (the part of the hand sacred to <s>Brahmā</s>). He wipes his mouth twice with the base of his thumb. <s>Agni</s> is the presiding deity of the thumb, <s>Vāyu</s> of the forefinger, <s>Prajāpati</s> of the middle finger, the <s>Sun</s> of the ring finger, and <s>Indra</s> of the little finger. He wipes his mouth with the thumb and middle finger, or with all the hand's sacred points; he touches his eyes with the thumb and ring finger, his nose with the thumb and forefinger, his ears and arms with the thumb and little finger, his heart with those two or with the thumb, his navel with the fingers, and each limb with the thumb, after touching water. Having also sprinkled his shanks and left hand, he touches his head with all the fingers. With the formula, ‘I am <s>Indra</s>, with both,’ he touches both hands; with ‘The Waters are the feet; in this family,’ he touches both feet. After similarly washing his feet, he again sips water in the same manner with the formula, ‘May the Waters purify.’ Saying, ‘May the <s>Ṛgveda</s> be satisfied; may the <s>Yajurveda</s> be satisfied; may the <s>Sāmaveda</s> be satisfied,’ he drinks water three times. Saying, ‘May the <s>Atharvaveda</s> be satisfied; may the <s>Itihāsaveda</s> be satisfied; may the <s>Moon</s> be satisfied,’ he wipes his mouth three times. With ‘May <s>Maheśvara</s> be satisfied,’ he touches his head; with ‘May the <s>Sun</s> be satisfied; may <s>Soma</s> be satisfied,’ his eyes; with ‘May the directions be satisfied,’ his ears; with ‘May <s>Vāyu</s> be satisfied,’ his nose; with ‘May <s>Indra</s> be satisfied,’ his arms; with ‘May <s>Viṣṇu</s> be satisfied,’ his heart; and with ‘May <s>Agni</s> be satisfied,’ his navel. So some authorities teach.

children.text: athāpo namaskṛtyāvagāhya yāvad amanaḥśaṅkam adbhirmṛdā ca gātraśuddhiṃ kṛtvā vastram ā daśāt sūditamiti nenekti gāyatryā prāgagrikam udagagrikaṃ vāstṛṇāti śuṣke tayaiva gṛhṇīyādidamāpaḥ pravahatetyabhigamya hiraṇyaśṛṅgamiti jalaṃ praṇamya samṛdodakenāpaḥ punātvityabhyukṣyedamāpaḥ śivā ity apo vigāhya susvātīdaṃ brahma punīmaha iti pavitraṃ gṛhītvā brahma punātvityaṅgulyāṃ nikṣipya śatadhāramiti jalaṃ gṛhītvā payasvatīroṣadhaya ityācamya bhūragnaya ityupasthānamādityasya citpatiriti tribhiranāmikopāntābhyāṃ samṛdodakena triḥ pradakṣiṇamāvartya śiro mārṣṭyāpohiraṇyapavamānaiḥ prokṣayatyud vayam ityādinādityamupasthāya mahāvyāhṛtyā jalamabhimantrya karṇāvapidhāyābhimukhamādityārdhaṃ nimajjya ṛtaṃ ca satyaṃ ca yāsu gandhā iti trirāvartayannaghamarṣaṇaṃ karoti tato mandaṃ niḥśvasya dhautaṃ paridhāyānupamṛjya vāsaḥ prātaḥ sūryaś cetyādinācamyāpohiṣṭhādibhir ṛgbhis tisṛbhiḥ prokṣya gāyatryāpo 'bhimantryādityābhimukhaṃ vikṣipya pradakṣiṇaṃ karoti prāṇāyāmamekāvaraṃ kṛtvāṣṭāvarāṃ sāvitrīmabhyasya mitrasyetyādibhir ṛgbhis tisṛbhis tiṣṭhansaṃdhyām upāsīta madhyāhna āpaḥ punantvityācamya tathā prokṣyod vayam ityādibhir yajurbhis tiṣṭhannādityam upasthāya tathā karoti sāyamagniścetyādinācamya tathā prokṣya yacciddhītyādibhiḥ sāmabhirupāsyāsīnastathā karotyuditārkāṃ paścimārkāmiti ca saṃdhye yathādiśaṃ tannāmādinā digdevatāḥ pitṝn sāpasavyaṃ brahmāṇaṃ codaṅmukho nārāyaṇādīnnamo 'ntenopatiṣṭheta ||
children.translated_text: Then, after bowing to the waters and entering them, he should cleanse his limbs with water and clay until no doubt remains in his mind. He washes the garment up to ten times with the formula “It has been purified” [reading uncertain]. With the <s>Gāyatrī</s> he spreads it out with its end toward the east or north; when it is dry, he should take it up with that same formula. Approaching the water with “These waters flow,” bowing to it with “Golden-horned,” and sprinkling himself with clay-mixed water with “May the waters purify,” he enters the waters with “These waters are auspicious.” With “Well purified, we purify this sacred power” he takes a <s>pavitra</s> (purifying ring), and with “May sacred power purify” places it on his finger. With “Hundred-streamed” he takes water, and with “The milk-rich plants” he sips it. He performs the attendance rite with “Earth, the fires.” With the three formulas beginning “The lord of consciousness of <s>Āditya</s>,” he uses the tips of his ring fingers to turn clay-mixed water clockwise three times and wipes his head. He sprinkles himself with the water, golden, and purifying verses, attends upon the sun with the formulas beginning “Upward we,” consecrates water with the great utterance, closes his ears, faces <s>Āditya</s>, and immerses half his body. Repeating three times “Truth and reality” and “In which are the fragrances,” he performs the sin-effacing rite. He then exhales gently, puts on the washed garment without wiping himself, and in the morning sips water with the formulas beginning “The sun and I.” After sprinkling himself with the three verses beginning “The waters are indeed,” he consecrates water with the <s>Gāyatrī</s>, casts it toward <s>Āditya</s>, and turns clockwise. Having performed one round of breath control and repeated the <s>Sāvitrī</s> eight times, he should stand and perform the twilight worship with the three verses beginning “Of <s>Mitra</s>.” At midday he sips water with “May the waters purify,” sprinkles himself in the same way, stands and attends upon <s>Āditya</s> with the sacrificial formulas beginning “Upward we,” and proceeds likewise. In the evening he sips water with the formulas beginning “The fire and I,” sprinkles himself likewise, worships with the chants beginning “Whatever indeed,” and, seated, proceeds in the same manner. At the two twilight junctions, called “the risen sun” and “the western sun,” he should honor the directional deities in their respective directions by formulas beginning with their names, the ancestors with the sacred thread over the right shoulder, <s>Brahmā</s>, and, while facing north, <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> and the others, using formulas ending in “homage.”

children.translated_text: Then, after sipping water, he bows to the water with “The field of the Kurus,” consecrates it with the great utterance, and offers libations with his hand in the prescribed sequence of the palm’s sacred places, using formulas beginning “To those of the wells, svāhā.” He offers satisfaction with the words: “I satisfy <s>Bhūpati</s>; I satisfy <s>Bhuvanapati</s>; I satisfy <s>Bhūtapati</s>; I satisfy <s>Prajāpati</s>; I satisfy <s>Brahmā</s>; I satisfy <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>; I satisfy <s>Mahādeva</s>; I satisfy <s>Skanda</s>; I satisfy <s>Vināyaka</s>.” He offers to the directional deities in their respective directions with formulas beginning with their names: “I satisfy <s>Indra</s>; I satisfy <s>Yama</s>; I satisfy <s>Varuṇa</s>; I satisfy <s>Kubera</s>; I satisfy <s>Agni</s>; I satisfy <s>Nirṛti</s>; I satisfy <s>Vāyu</s>; I satisfy <s>Īśāna</s>.” He continues: “I satisfy <s>Āditya</s>; I satisfy <s>Soma</s>; I satisfy <s>Aṅgāraka</s>; I satisfy <s>Budha</s>; I satisfy <s>Bṛhaspati</s>; I satisfy <s>Śukra</s>; I satisfy <s>Śanaiścara</s>; I satisfy <s>Rāhu</s>; I satisfy <s>Ketu</s>; I satisfy the planets; I satisfy the lunar mansions; I satisfy the stars; I satisfy all the gods; I satisfy every deity; I satisfy the Vedas; I satisfy the sacrifices; I satisfy the metres.” He then satisfies the seven seers associated with his own lineage: “I satisfy <s>Viśvāmitra</s>; I satisfy <s>Jamadagni</s>; I satisfy <s>Bharadvāja</s>; I satisfy <s>Gautama</s>; I satisfy <s>Atri</s>; I satisfy <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>; I satisfy <s>Kaśyapa</s>; I satisfy <s>Bhṛgu</s>.” Wearing the sacred thread over the right shoulder, he performs the ancestral rites. With the formula beginning “At the boundary of wave and water,” he offers satisfaction to the fathers, grandfathers, great-grandfathers, groups of kinsmen, wives of the fathers, wives of the grandfathers, wives of the great-grandfathers, and wives of the groups of kinsmen, saying to each, “With <s>svadhā</s>, homage; I satisfy you.” Then, wearing the thread around his neck, he says: “I satisfy the terrestrial beings; I satisfy the terrestrial divinities; I satisfy the <s>Nāgas</s>; I satisfy the divine <s>Nāgas</s>.” With “May all who desire water, however many they are, receive it,” he releases the water, sips water, and performs the <s>brahmayajña</s> (daily Vedic recitation). In a clean place he spreads sacrificial grass, takes the seat of sacred recitation, holds a purifier in his hand, forms the gesture of the joined hands for sacred recitation, and faces east. Regularly he should recite, preceded by the <s>Sāvitrī</s>, passages beginning “For refreshment, for strength,” as desired. On special occasions he should perform personal recitation of passages beginning “Truth and reality,” “Of what was done by the gods,” “What crosses within my womb,” “He, the exhilarator,” “The purifier of <s>Vasu</s>,” “For <s>Jātavedas</s>,” “Now of <s>Viṣṇu</s>,” “Thousand-headed,” the single syllable, “I have brought you,” and “You, <s>Agni</s>, purify,” and others. With solar verses, as desired, he should also attend upon <s>Āditya</s>.

children.text: aśakto nityaṃ pādau prakṣālyācamya ato devādi vaiṣṇavaṃ japtvā divyaṃ vāyavyamāgneyaṃ mantrasnānaṃ vā kṛtvā pūrvavadācamanādīni kuryāddivaścyutairgāṅgeyairādhāvaiḥ sātapair varṣair vāsecanaṃ divyaṃ gavāṃ pādodgatairvāyunītaiḥ pāṃsubhiḥ sparśanaṃ vāyavyaṃ bhasmanā śuddhena sarvāṅgamālepanamāgneyamāpo hi ṣṭheti mantreṇāgneyena tīrthenābhyukṣaṇaṃ mantrasnānaṃ dakṣiṇapāṇermadhyatalamāgneyaṃ tīrthaṃ kaniṣṭhāṅgulimūlaṃ daivaṃ sarvāṅgulimūlāgramārṣaṃ pradeśinyaṅguṣṭhayormadhyaṃ paitṛkamaṅguṣṭhasya mūlaṃ brāhmaṃ daivena tīrthenopavītī daivikaṃ kāryamārṣeṇārṣaṃ paitṛkeṇa pitryaṃ sarvaṃ brāhmeṇa brahmatarpaṇamācamanamāgneyena tīrthenābhyukṣaṇaṃ karoti dakṣiṇahastamuddhṛtyopavītaṃ dhārayedupavītī vāmamuddhṛtya prācīnāvītī kaṇṭhasakte nivītī bhavati snātvā puṇye 'hani saṃskārahomaṃ juhuyāditi vijñāyate ||
children.translated_text: One who is unable to perform a full bath should every day wash his feet, sip water, recite the Vaiṣṇava formula beginning <s>ato devāḥ</s>, and perform either the celestial, aerial, fiery, or mantra-bath; he should then perform sipping and the other acts as before. Sprinkling oneself with waters fallen from the sky—with waters of <s>Gaṅgā</s>, running waters, sun-warmed waters, or rainwater—is the celestial bath. Contact with dust raised by cows’ feet and borne by the wind is the aerial bath. Smearing the entire body with pure ash is the fiery bath. Sprinkling oneself with the mantra <s>āpo hi ṣṭhā</s>, using the fiery <s>tīrtha</s> (sacred part of the hand), is the mantra-bath. The middle of the right palm is the fiery <s>tīrtha</s>; the root of the little finger is the divine one; the region from the roots to the tips of all the fingers is the seers’ one; the space between the index finger and thumb is the ancestral one; and the root of the thumb is the Brāhma one. Wearing the sacred thread over the left shoulder, he performs a divine act with the divine <s>tīrtha</s>, a seers’ act with the seers’ one, and an ancestral act with the ancestral one. He performs all libations to <s>Brahman</s> and sipping with the Brāhma one, and sprinkling with the fiery <s>tīrtha</s>. He should raise his right arm and put on the sacred thread, thus becoming an <s>upavītin</s>; by raising the left arm he becomes a <s>prācīnāvītin</s>, with the thread worn in reverse; when it rests around his neck he is a <s>nivītin</s>. After bathing, he should offer a consecratory fire-oblation on an auspicious day—so it is understood.

children.text: atha puṇyāhaṃ pañcāvarāñchrotriyān āhūyābhipūjayatyācāryaḥ karakaṃ dhārāsvity adbhir āpūryedam āpaḥ śivā ity apo 'bhimantrya puṣpādyaiḥ sarvatīrthajalam ityabhyarcya prativācakān prāṅmukhān udaṅmukhān vā sthāpayitvodaṅmukhaḥ supuṇyāhaṃ karomīti saṃkalpya svasti suprokṣitamastviti sthānaṃ prokṣya prajāpatiḥ priyatām ityuktvā taiḥ priyatām iti vācayati śāmyantu ghorāṇītyuttarāntaṃ trir apaḥ srāvayati ato devā ityagraṃ daivike saṃ tvā siñcāmītyagraṃ sūtake śucī vo havyetyagraṃ pretake draviṇodāḥ savitā navo navo vidyucchataṃ jīvāṣṭau devā hiraṇyarūpa ṛdhyāma stomamāhārṣaṃ tvāryamaṇaṃ somam rājānam indrāvaruṇā śriye jāto yā guṅguryastvā hṛdā yasmai tvaṃ narya prajāṃ sutrāmāṇaṃ śatāyudhāya dakṣiṇāvatāṃ bhadraṃ karṇebhiḥ śataminnv aditir dyaur ityṛtvijaḥ sarve vadeyuḥ ||
children.translated_text: Next, for the <s>puṇyāha</s> (auspicious-day rite), he invites and duly honors no fewer than five learned <s>śrotriyas</s>. The teacher fills a pitcher with water while reciting <s>dhārāsu</s>, consecrates the water with <s>idam āpaḥ śivāḥ</s>, and worships it with flowers and the other offerings while saying, “Water of all sacred bathing places.” Having stationed the respondents facing east or north, he himself faces north, resolves, “I shall perform the excellent <s>puṇyāha</s>,” and sprinkles the place, saying, “May there be well-being; may it be well sprinkled.” After saying, “May <s>Prajāpati</s> be pleased,” he has them respond, “May he be pleased.” Beginning with <s>śāmyantu ghorāṇi</s> and continuing through the end of the following formula, he lets water flow three times. In a rite for a deity he uses the passage beginning <s>ato devāḥ</s>; at a birth impurity, that beginning <s>saṃ tvā siñcāmi</s>; and at a death impurity, that beginning <s>śucī vo havyā</s>. All the officiating priests should recite the passages beginning <s>draviṇodāḥ</s>, <s>savitā</s>, <s>navo navaḥ</s>, <s>vidyuc chataṃ jīva</s>, <s>aṣṭau devāḥ</s>, <s>hiraṇyarūpaḥ</s>, <s>ṛdhyāma</s>, <s>stomam</s>, <s>āhārṣaṃ tvā</s>, <s>Aryamaṇam</s>, <s>Somam rājānam</s>, <s>Indrāvaruṇā</s>, <s>śriye jātaḥ</s>, <s>yā guṅgūḥ</s>, <s>yas tvā hṛdā</s>, <s>yasmai tvam</s>, <s>narya prajām</s>, <s>sutrāmāṇam</s>, <s>śatāyudhāya</s>, <s>dakṣiṇāvatām</s>, <s>bhadraṃ karṇebhiḥ</s>, <s>śatam in nu</s>, and <s>Aditir dyauḥ</s>.

children.text: devā ṛṣayaḥ pitaro grahā devya ṛṣipatnyaḥ pitṛpatnyo vedā yajñāśca sarvādyāḥ priyantāmantaḥ prativacanaṃ puṇyāhaṃ śivam āyuṣyam arogyam avighnam acalam aiśvaryaṃ yatpāpaṃ tatpratihataṃ yacchreyaḥ śivaṃ karma śivaḥ pakṣa ityastvantāstathāntaḥ prativacanaṃ śivā ṛtavaḥ santu śivāni nakṣatrāṇi bhavantu sarvakarmasamṛddhirastu sarvadhanadhānyasampūrṇam astvityekaikam uktavantaḥ prativacanaṃ yatpuṇyaṃ svasti na ṛdhyāsmeti pūrvoktāmitare 'nuvadanti yajamānasya nakṣatranāmādi gotranāma sutāntaṃ mātṛgotranāmāntātparaṃ śarmāntaṃ nāma praṇavādi bhavanto bruvantu puṇyāhaṃ svastyṛddhyantaṃ pratyekaṃ tridhā tridhā yathāvibhaktivācitamanuvācayeyuḥ āpohiraṇyapavamānaiḥ prokṣayati puṇyāhe kṛte tadahaḥ puṇyaṃ bhavatyādāvante vā puṇyāhena sarvāḥ kriyāḥ puṇyāḥ paripūrṇā bhavanti svāṃkṛto 'sīti dakṣiṇākālamuktavatsu ghṛtāt parītyadbhir yathāśakti dakṣiṇāṃ hastena dakṣiṇena dadāti tvamagne yajñānām hoteti tadādadīranyatra dakṣiṇādānādāne tatraivaṃ syāditi vijñāyate ||
children.translated_text: “May the gods, seers, ancestors, planets, goddesses, wives of the seers, wives of the ancestors, the <s>Vedas</s>, sacrifices, and all beings beginning with these be pleased”: the response ends with “May they be pleased.” The declarations—“May this be an auspicious day; may there be welfare, longevity, health, freedom from obstacles, stability, and sovereignty; may whatever sin there is be repelled; may what is excellent be auspicious; may the rite be auspicious; may the fortnight be auspicious”—all end with “May it be so,” and the response likewise ends with “So be it.” After each declaration, “May the seasons be favorable; may the lunar mansions be favorable; may every rite prosper; may there be complete abundance of all wealth and grain,” there is a response. When one has said, “Whatever merit there is—may there be well-being for us; may we prosper,” the others repeat the preceding words. He states the sacrificer’s lunar-mansion name and so forth, his <s>gotra</s>-name, and the name ending in “son”; after the maternal <s>gotra</s>-name, the following name ends in <s>śarman</s>. Beginning with <s>oṃ</s>, he says, “Venerable sirs, pronounce the auspicious day,” and, successively through the declarations of well-being and prosperity, he has them repeat each expression three times in its appropriate grammatical form. He sprinkles with the <s>Āpaḥ</s>, <s>Hiraṇya</s>, and <s>Pavamāna</s> verses. When the <s>puṇyāha</s> has been performed, that day becomes auspicious; when a <s>puṇyāha</s> is performed at the beginning or end, all rites become auspicious and complete. When they have uttered <s>svāṃkṛto ’si</s> at the time for the fee, he recites <s>ghṛtāt parī</s> and gives, with his right hand, water and a fee according to his means. They should accept it while saying, <s>tvam Agne yajñānāṃ hotā</s>. Where no fee is either given or accepted, the procedure should be just so—thus it is understood.

children.text: athāgnyāyatanaṃ prākpravaṇe vottarapravaṇe vā śuddhe deśe gomayenopalipte śuddhābhiḥ sikatābhiḥ prākpaścimaṃ dakṣiṇottaraṃ ca dvātriṃśadaṅgulyāyataṃ dvyaṅgulonnataṃ yathālābhonnataṃ vā sthaṇḍilamagnyāyatanaṃ bhavati paristaraṇabarhiṣaḥ pratidik pañcadaśa sthaṇḍilapramāṇāḥ kuṇḍe ṣaṭtriṃśadaṅgulāstathaikāṅgulipariṇāhā vraṇavakrahīnāḥ paridhayaḥ pañcadaśadarbhairgrathitaṃ caturaṅgulāgraṃ dvyaṅgulagranthi hastamātraṃ prokṣaṇakūrcaṃ tathaiva dvādaśāṅgulamātraṃ pavitraṃ tatpramāṇā yājñikāḥ samidhaḥ pātrasruvādayo yajñe proktā darbheṣu dvaṃdvaṃ pātrādisambhārānuttare daivike pratyekaṃ dakṣiṇataḥ paitṛke saṃbharati nityahome 'gniśālāyāṃ mṛdā caturdiśaṃ dvātriṃśadaṅgulyāyatāṃ caturaṅgulavistārāṃ dvyaṅgulonnatāmūrdhvavediṃ caturaṅgulivistāronnatāṃ tatparigatām adhovediṃ ca madhye nimnaṃ ṣaḍaṅgulamagnikuṇḍaṃ kṛtvāsmin gṛhastho 'gnimaupāsanamādhāya nityaṃ juhoti vanasthasya śrāmaṇakāgreḥ kuṇḍam ādhānaviśeṣaṃ ca dharme vakṣyāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Next comes the site of the fire. On clean ground sloping eastward or northward and plastered with cow dung, a <s>sthaṇḍila</s> (raised fire platform) is made with clean sand, extending thirty-two finger-breadths east to west and south to north and rising two finger-breadths, or as high as circumstances permit; this is the site of the fire. The strewing grasses number fifteen in each direction and are of the measure of the <s>sthaṇḍila</s>; for a fire pit they are thirty-six finger-breadths. The enclosing sticks are one finger-breadth in circumference and free from wounds and crookedness. The sprinkling bundle is tied from fifteen <s>darbha</s> blades, has tips four finger-breadths long, a knot of two finger-breadths, and is one hand in length. The purifier is made in the same way and is twelve finger-breadths long. The sacrificial fuel sticks have that same measure. Vessels, ladles, and the other items prescribed for a sacrifice are arranged in pairs upon <s>darbha</s> grass: to the north for a divine rite and individually to the south for an ancestral rite. For the daily fire-offering, in the fire hall he constructs with clay an upper altar extending thirty-two finger-breadths on each of the four sides, four finger-breadths wide, and two finger-breadths high; around it is a lower altar four finger-breadths wide and high. In the center he makes a fire pit sunken six finger-breadths. Having established the domestic <s>aupāsana</s> fire in it, the householder offers into it every day. We shall explain in the section on <s>dharma</s> the fire pit for the forest-dweller’s <s>śrāmaṇaka</s> fire and the special procedure for its establishment.

children.text: athāghāravidhānaṃ brāhmaṃ prāṅmukham āsīna eto nvindramityagnyālayaṃ prokṣya mayi devā ityādibhiścaturdiśaṃ darbhānukṣayed uddhanyamānamiti madhyapūrvāparayamāgninirṛtisomeśānamaruto barhiṣā khanati tathā pūta hyātaneti ṣaḍrekhā likhitvāṣṭābandham iti vakritaṃ darbhaṃ dakṣiṇapaścimasyāmutsṛjya rekhā gāyatryā prokṣya jātavedo bhuvanasyetyaraṇiṃ gṛhītvā mathitaṃ laukikaṃ vāgnimādāyāhareta ghṛtapratīka iti prajvālyāyurdā iti praṇamyopāvaroheti nidhāyāgna āyāhyayaṃ te yoniriti prajvālya mayi gṛhṇāmītyabhivandya karmaṇe vāmiti karau prakṣālayati idamāpaḥ śivā ity apo 'bhimantryādite 'numanyasva dakṣiṇato vediṃ parimṛjāmīti dakṣiṇavediṃ nairṛtyādyantamanumate 'numanyasva paścimato vediṃ parimṛjāmīti tathā paścimavediṃ sarasvate 'numanyasvottarato vediṃ parimṛjāmītyuttaravediṃ vāyavyādyantaṃ deva savitaḥ prasuva purastādvediṃ parimṛjāmīti pūrvavediṃ cāgneyādyantam aṅgulīrāstīrya sādhāvena pāṇinā kūrcena vā parimṛjya gāyatryā vedīḥ prokṣayati brahmasomāvṛtvijau varayitvādhvaryuroṃ bhūpate bhuvanapata iti pratyekaṃ prekṣya tābhyāmahaṃ bhūpatirityukte brahman soma prokṣiṣyāmītyantaṃ tathoktvā punastābhyāṃ prokṣetyuktas tathā prokṣayati ||
children.translated_text: Now follows the procedure for the āghāra (preliminary libation). Sitting in the Brahman's position facing east, he sprinkles the fireplace with the formula beginning “Come now to Indra,” and with the formulas beginning “The gods in me” he sprinkles darbha grass toward the four directions. With “Being raised up,” he scrapes with sacrificial grass at the center and in the regions of the east, west, Yama, Agni, Nirṛti, Soma, Īśāna, and the Maruts. Having likewise drawn six lines with “For it is purified by that,” he casts a bent blade of grass into the southwest with “The eightfold bond.” He sprinkles the lines with the Gāyatrī. Taking the fire sticks with “O Jātavedas, of the world,” he obtains fire either kindled by friction or taken from an ordinary fire and brings it forward. He makes it blaze with “Whose face is ghee,” bows to it with “Giver of life,” deposits it with “Descend,” and kindles it with “Come, O Agni</s; this is your womb.” He reverences it with “I receive [you] within me” and washes his hands with “For the rite, you two.” He consecrates the water with “These waters are auspicious.” Saying, “Consent, O Aditi; I wipe the altar on the south,” he wipes the southern side of the altar, beginning and ending in the southwest. In the same way, saying, “Consent, O Anumati; I wipe the altar on the west,” he wipes its western side. Saying, “Consent, O Sarasvatī; I wipe the altar on the north,” he wipes its northern side, beginning and ending in the northwest. Saying, “Impel it, divine Savitṛ; I wipe the altar on the east,” he wipes its eastern side, beginning and ending in the southeast. Spreading his fingers, he wipes the altar with his lowered hand or with a bundle of grass, and sprinkles its sides with the Gāyatrī. Having chosen the Brahman and Soma as officiating priests, the Adhvaryu looks at each in turn and says, “Oṃ, lord of the earth; lord of the world.” When they have respectively replied, “I am lord of the earth” and so forth, he similarly addresses them through the words, “O Brahman, O Soma, I am about to sprinkle.” When each again tells him, “Sprinkle,” he sprinkles accordingly.

children.text: pātrādādhāvamādāya pavitre stha iti vedyāṃ barhiṣaḥ sthāpayitvā tānparaśurasīti prokṣya samidho muktabandhāḥ kṛṣṇo 'sīti vedirasīti vediṃ sruvādīnbarhiṣo barhirasi srugbhya iti barhiṣo 'graṃ dive tveti madhyamantarikṣāyeti mūlaṃ pṛthivyai tveti prokṣayati poṣāya tvety apo barhirbandhane saṃsrāvya svadhā pitṛbhya iti sāpasavyaṃ dakṣiṇataḥ prokṣyāpāṃ śeṣaṃ paścimasyām uttarāntamūrgbhaveti srāvayedubhābhyāmiti pāṇī prakṣālayati pūṣā ta iti barhirbandhaṃ visṛjya mūlād ūrdhvamādityaṃ vyañjanamasītyabhimṛśya paścimato vedyadhastāduttarāgram ūrṇāmradasamiti darbhaiḥ paristīrya svāsasthaṃ devebhya iti prāgagraṃ svāsane caikaṃ nidhāya viṣṇoḥ stūpo 'sīti prācyāṃ dakṣiṇata iti yāmyāmuttarata ityudīcyāṃ paścimata iti pratīcyāṃ prāguttarāgraṃ paristṛṇātyuttarāgram aiśānyām ūrdhvaṃ kṛtvā gandharvo 'sīti paścimasyāmindrasyeti yāmyāṃ mitrāvaruṇāvityudīcyāṃ vedyāṃ prāguttarāgrānparidhīnparidadhāti ||
children.translated_text: Taking the rinsing water from the vessel, he places the sacrificial grass on the altar with “You are purifiers,” and sprinkles it with “You are an axe.” He then sprinkles the unbound fuel sticks with “You are black,” the altar with “You are the altar,” the ladle and the other implements, and the sacrificial grass: its tip with “You are the grass for the offering-spoons,” its middle with “For heaven,” and its root with “For the atmosphere” and “For the earth.” With “For prosperity” he lets water flow onto the binding of the grass. Saying, “<s>Svadhā</s> to the ancestors,” he sprinkles southward, moving counterclockwise; with “Become nourishment,” he pours the remaining water on the western side as far as its northern end. With “With both,” he washes his hands. He loosens the binding of the grass with “<s>Pūṣan</s> is yours,” then, touching it upward from the root, says, “You are the distinguishing mark of <s>Āditya</s>.” To the west, below the altar, he spreads <s>darbha</s> grass with its tips northward, using “Soft as wool.” With “A good seat for the gods,” he lays one east-pointing blade upon the seat. With “You are <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s crest” in the east, “From the south” in the south, “From the north” in the north, and “From the west” in the west, he strews grass around the altar with its tips toward the east and north. In the northeast he raises the northward-pointing tip. On the altar he places the enclosing sticks with their tips toward the east and north: on the western side with “You are the <s>Gandharva</s>,” on the southern with “Of <s>Indra</s>,” and on the northern with “<s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>.”

children.text: vāyavyāmuttarāgram ūrdhvaṃ karoti sūryastveti prācyām uttarāntam upariṣṭād ityūrdhvam adhastānnāgā ityadhaśca pariṣicya vītihotramityagnyālaye samidhāvagnīśayordiśor ūrdhvāgre nidadhāti paristīryamityādinaindrādyam udagantam ārṣeṇāpo dattvā sṛtāsītyādibhirdakṣiṇādi tenaiva prāgantam uttarāntaṃ ca pariṣicya taruṇāsīty āgneyādīśānāntaṃ pradakṣiṇam āgneyāntam adbhiḥ pariṣiñcati vānaspatyo 'sīti praṇidhī prakṣālya pṛthivyāpo grahīṣyāmīti sākṣatam adbhirāpūrya vasūnāṃ pavitramityudagagre pavitre prakṣipya dakṣiṇena pāṇināgramitaradvāmena gṛhītvā devo vaḥ saviteti trirutpūya tathā nidadhāti brahmann apa iti somāya iti ca brahmasomāvṛtvijau pratyekaṃ prekṣya tābhyāṃ tathā praṇayetyuktaḥ ko va iti praṇīya vedyāṃ dakṣiṇottarayoḥ praṇidhī nidhāya saṃviśantāmiti kūrcena jalaṃ saṃsrāvya gāyatryā sruvaṃ prokṣayet ||
children.translated_text: In the northwest he raises the northward-pointing tip. On the eastern side, at its northern end, he sprinkles above with “The <s>Sun</s> [protects] you” and “From above,” and below with “The <s>Nāgas</s> from below.” With “The bearer of the oblation,” he places two fuel sticks in the fireplace, their tips raised, in the directions of <s>Agni</s> and <s>Īśāna</s>. Beginning with the eastern quarter belonging to <s>Indra</s> and ending in the north, he offers water with the formulas beginning “To be spread around” and with the formula of the seer. With the formulas beginning “You have gone forth,” he sprinkles from the south onward by the same course as far as the east and finally the north. With “You are young,” he then sprinkles water clockwise from the southeast through the northeast and back to the southeast. With “You are of the forest tree,” he rinses the two water vessels. Saying, “I shall take the waters of the earth,” he fills them with water containing grains of rice. With “The purifier of the <s>Vasus</s>,” he places in them two purifying blades whose tips point north. Holding their tips with his right hand and their other ends with his left, he strains the water three times with “May the god <s>Savitṛ</s> purify you,” and replaces the purifiers in the same manner. Looking separately toward the <s>Brahman</s> and <s>Soma</s> priests, he says, “O <s>Brahman</s>, the waters,” and “For <s>Soma</s>.” When they tell him, “Bring them forward in that manner,” he carries the waters forward with “Who [brings] you?” He sets the two vessels on the southern and northern sides of the altar, causes their water to mingle with a bundle of grass while saying, “Let them unite,” and sprinkles the dipping ladle with the <s>Gāyatrī</s>.

children.text: bhūḥ sruvaṃ gṛhṇāmīti sruvaṃ gṛhītvā varṣiṣṭhe adhi nāka iti vedyadhastātsamidhau nyasyāhīno nirvapāmīti sruvaṃ prakṣālya nirdagdhamiti paryagniṃ kṛtvā niṣṭaptamiti samidhor nidadhyād aditir asyacchidretyājyasthālīṃ gṛhītvottare bhūtakṛtaḥ sthopoḍham ityaṅgāraṃ nyasya sagarāḥ stheti vinyasya mahīnāmiti pacati pūrvavatpavitreṇa trirutpūyājyasthālyāḥ pṛṣṭhabhasmedaṃ viṣṇuriti vedena śodhayitvodbhavaḥ sthod ahamiti barhirdagdhvāṅgāramantaritamityājyasya darśayati dakṣiṇato 'ṅgāraṃ gāyatryā nyasya tayaiva carusthālīmadhiśritya darbholkena paktvāvatārayati pavitreṇājyaṃ pātre trirutpūya gharmo 'sīti granthiṃ visṛjyottarapaścime nidhāyādbhiḥ prokṣyāpyāyantāmiti pavitraṃ juhoti vītihotramiti samidagraṃ ghṛtāktaṃ vāyavye 'gnau sthāpayitvā devasya tveti sruveṇa homyaṃ dvidhā viharati ||
children.translated_text: Having taken the <s>sruva</s> (offering ladle) with the words, “<s>Bhūḥ</s>; I take the ladle,” he places it on a fuel stick beneath the altar with “Upon the highest vault.” He rinses the ladle with “Unfailing, I pour out,” passes it around the fire with “Burned away,” and lays it upon the two fuel sticks with “Heated through.” Taking the vessel for clarified butter with “This is <s>Aditi</s>, unbroken,” he places it to the north. With “You are makers of beings; brought near,” he puts down an ember, arranges it with “You are accompanied by the oceans,” and cooks with “Of the great ones.” As before, he strains the clarified butter three times with the <s>pavitra</s> (strainer). With “This is <s>Viṣṇu</s>,” he cleans the ash from the outside of the butter vessel with the <s>veda</s> (ritual grass bundle). Having burned sacrificial grass with “You rise up; I rise,” he shows the ember to the clarified butter with “Placed between.” He deposits the ember to the south with the <s>Gāyatrī</s>, sets the vessel for the <s>caru</s> (cooked oblation) over it with that same verse, cooks with a blazing bundle of <s>darbha</s> grass, and takes the vessel down. He strains the clarified butter three times into a vessel with the <s>pavitra</s>. With “You are heat,” he loosens its knot, places it to the northwest, and sprinkles it with water. With “May they increase,” he offers the <s>pavitra</s> into the fire. With “Whose oblation has been conveyed,” he places the ghee-smeared tip of a fuel stick in the northwestern part of the fire; then, with “For the god, you,” he divides the substance to be offered into two portions with the ladle.

children.text: dakṣiṇapraṇidhau brāhmeṇa tīrthena prajāpatipurogān āvāhayāmītyuttarapraṇidhau daivenāgnyādīnaupāsanayajñaṃ yajñadaivataviśvān devān sarvadevān āvāhayāmītyantaṃ paitṛke vaiśvadevayajñaṃ yajñadaivataviśvān devān āvāhayāmītyantam āvāhayed yathāvāhanaṃ sruveṇājyam ūrdhvaṃ nītvā juṣṭaṃ nirvapāmīti nirvāpaṃ karoti tṛpyadhidvayena dvidhāgnau homyaṃ darśayitvāgnirjyotirdvayena samidulkena dvidhā dahati samidasi svāheti samidhaṃ juhoti sruveṇājyaṃ gṛhītvāmṛtamasīti anuttānam antaritam ityuttānaṃ pratyuṣṭam ityanuttānaṃ homyaṃ pradakṣiṇamabhimantryājyaṃ gṛhītvottānaṃ svato dakṣiṇato vāmataḥ praṇītāyāṃ saṃdhāya citpatistvādibhistribhireva tridhāgnau saṃvapati ||
children.translated_text: At the southern <s>praṇidhi</s> (ritual deposit), using the part of the hand sacred to <s>Brahmā</s>, he says, “I invoke those headed by <s>Prajāpati</s>.” At the northern deposit, using the part sacred to the gods, he invokes those beginning with <s>Agni</s>, ending with “I invoke the <s>aupāsana</s> sacrifice, the <s>Viśve Devas</s> who are the deities of the sacrifice, and all the gods.” In the ancestral rite he should invoke them from “the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> sacrifice” through “I invoke the <s>Viśve Devas</s> who are the deities of the sacrifice.” In the order in which they were invoked, he raises clarified butter with the ladle and performs the setting-down with “I set down what has been graciously accepted.” With the pair of formulas beginning with the textually uncertain word <s>tṛpyadhi</s>, he shows the offering to the fire in two portions; with the pair beginning “<s>Agni</s> is light,” he burns the two portions with a blazing fuel stick. He offers the fuel stick with “You are a fuel stick, <s>svāhā</s>.” Taking clarified butter with the ladle, he moves the offering clockwise while consecrating it—face-down with “You are nectar,” face-up with “Placed between,” and face-down with “Burned forward.” Taking clarified butter, he places it face-up in the consecrated water, successively on his own side, on the right, and on the left; with the three formulas beginning “The lord of thought takes you,” he pours it into the fire in three portions.

children.text: gāyatryā samidhaḥ prokṣyaikaviṃśatirāhutipramāṇāḥ karasampūrṇā vā samidho gṛhītvā mūlāgrābhyāṃ ghṛtaṃ sparśayitvābhyarcyākṣatājyacarubhirimā me agna iti mūlamadhyāgrāṇi spṛśannadho nītvordhvabhāge madhye ca saṃdadhāti daivena tīrthena dakṣiṇasyām adbhiḥ prāgantam adite 'numanyasveti paścimasyāmuttarāntamanumate 'numanyasvetyuttarasyāṃ prāgantaṃ sarasvate 'numanyasveti deva savitaḥ prasuveti pūrvasyāmudagantam āgneyādyantaṃ sarvataśca pradakṣiṇaṃ pariṣiñcati ṣaṣṭiṃ śatety abhimantryāyaṃ ta idhma itīdhmān asaṃkulāñcharo 'ṅgāre 'gnau juhuyādyasyai devatāyai havirnirupyate tāṃ devatāṃ manasā ha vai dhyāyannirvapedyathā ha vāsya suṣumnā jyotiṣmatī prāṇavatī retodhā ityetā hutaṃ gṛhītvā raśmayaś catasraḥ pṛśnau saṃdadhīran sa ha vā śuddhāmṛtavahā cinuhī divyā lokapāvanītyetābhiścandramasamāpyāyayatyasau nu rājā soma āpyāyito mūlagāmī vapāyany amṛtodgārī surapriyetyetābhir amṛtena tāṃ devatāṃ tarpayati ||
children.translated_text: Having sprinkled the fuel sticks with the <s>Gāyatrī</s>, he takes twenty-one sticks, each of the measure of an oblation, or as many as fill the hand. He touches clarified butter with their roots and tips and honors them with unbroken grains, clarified butter, and the cooked oblation. Reciting “These of mine, O <s>Agni</s>,” and touching their roots, middles, and tips, he lowers them and places them together in the upper part and the middle of the fire. With water from the part of the hand sacred to the gods, he sprinkles clockwise: along the southern side toward the east with “<s>Aditi</s>, give your assent”; along the western side toward the north with “<s>Anumati</s>, give your assent”; along the northern side toward the east with “<s>Sarasvatī</s>, give your assent”; and along the eastern side toward the north with “God <s>Savitṛ</s>, impel.” Thus he sprinkles all around, beginning and ending in the southeast. After consecrating them with the formula beginning “Sixty, a hundred,” he should offer the fuel sticks into the fire upon the embers, without crowding them, with “This is your kindling.” While setting down an oblation for a particular deity, he should mentally contemplate that deity. With the formulas “Just as <s>Suṣumnā</s> is luminous, endowed with vital breath, and seed-bearing,” the four rays, taking up what has been offered, should unite it in <s>Pṛśni</s>. With the formulas “Purified, carrying nectar, gather it up, O divine purifier of worlds,” he causes the moon to increase. With the formulas “That king <s>Soma</s>, replenished, goes to the root, nourishes the body, pours forth nectar, and is dear to the gods,” he satisfies that deity with nectar.

children.text: sruveṇājyaṃ srāvayanparidhī spṛṣṭvā vāyavyādyāgneyāntaṃ prajāpataye svāheti nairṛtyādīśānāntamindrāya svāhetyāghārau juhuyāccakṣuṣī buddhvāgnaye svāhā somāya svāhetyājyabhāgāvuttaradakṣiṇayorjuhoti yukto vaheti paścimādisaumyāntaṃ yā tiraścīti saumyādīndrāntaṃ saṃrādhanyai devyai svāhetīndrādiyāmyāntaṃ prasādhanyai devyai svāheti yāmyādivāruṇāntaṃ srāvayan hutvā madhyamāsyam iti buddhvā tatra vyāhṛtīrjuhoti tadagnimukhamiti brahmavādino vadanti satyenetyabhimṛśyājyena juhotyagnaye svāhā somāya svāhāgnīṣomābhyāṃ svāhā prajāpataye svāhā brahmaṇe svāhendrāya svāhā vasubhyaḥ svāhā marudbhyaḥ svāhā rudrebhyaḥ svāhā viṣṇave svāhā bṛhaspataye svāhā mitrāya svāhā varuṇāya svāhādityebhyaḥ svāhāśvibhyāṃ svāhā pūṣṇe svāhā kakṣāya svāhā kakṣadaivatasomāya svāhaupāsanayajñāya svāhā yajñadaivataviśvebhyo devebhyaḥ svāhā sarvadevebhyaḥ svāhetyantaṃ hutvā darvyābhighārya caruṃ sāvitryā gṛhītvā juhvā vyāhṛtīrjuhoti ato devā idaṃ viṣṇurityājyaṃ samṛddhyai juhuyātpaitṛke vaiśvadevayajñāya svāhā yajñadaivataviśvebhyo devebhyaḥ svāhetyantaṃ hutvā pakvaṃ juhuyāditi sarvahomānāmādirāghāro vijñāyate ||
children.translated_text: Letting clarified butter stream from the ladle and touching the enclosing sticks, he should offer the two āghāra (introductory libations): from northwest to southeast with “To Prajāpati, svāhā,” and from southwest to northeast with “To Indra, svāhā.” Regarding these as the two eyes, he offers the two portions of clarified butter on the northern and southern sides with “To Agni, svāhā” and “To Soma, svāhā.” Keeping the stream flowing, he offers from west to north with “Harnessed, convey”; from north to east with “She who goes crosswise”; from east to south with “To the goddess Saṃrādhanī, svāhā”; and from south to west with “To the goddess Prasādhanī, svāhā.” Understanding the center to be the mouth, he offers the great utterances there. The expounders of sacred knowledge call that the mouth of Agni. Touching it with the formula beginning “By truth,” he offers clarified butter: “To Agni, svāhā; to Soma, svāhā; to Agni and Soma, svāhā; to Prajāpati, svāhā; to Brahmā, svāhā; to Indra, svāhā; to the Vasus, svāhā; to the Maruts, svāhā; to the Rudras, svāhā; to Viṣṇu, svāhā; to Bṛhaspati, svāhā; to Mitra, svāhā; to Varuṇa, svāhā; to the Ādityas, svāhā; to the two Aśvins, svāhā; to Pūṣan, svāhā; to Kakṣa, svāhā; to Soma, the deity of Kakṣa, svāhā; to the aupāsana sacrifice, svāhā; to the Viśve Devas who are deities of the sacrifice, svāhā; to all the gods, svāhā</s.” After offering through the end of this series, he pours clarified butter over the cooked oblation with the large ladle, takes it with the offering ladle while reciting the Sāvitrī, and offers the great utterances. For prosperity, he should offer clarified butter with the formulas “From this the gods” and “This Viṣṇu.” In the ancestral rite, after offering through “To the Vaiśvadeva sacrifice, svāhā; to the Viśve Devas who are deities of the sacrifice, svāhā,” he should offer the cooked food. Thus the āghāra is understood to be the beginning of all fire offerings.

children.text: atha sāmānyataḥ kriyāyā homamantrāḥ dhātā dadātu no rayiṃ dhātā prajāyā dhātā dadātu no rayiṃ prācīṃ dhātā dadātu dāśuṣe 'nu no 'dyānumatir anvid anumate tvamā mā vājasya samāvavarttyanumanyatāṃ yasyāmidaṃ rākāmahaṃ yāste rāke sinīvāli yā supāṇiḥ kuhūmahuṃ kuhūrdevānāmiti dhātādi ṣoḍaśa ||
children.translated_text: Next, in general, the oblation-mantras for a rite are: “May <s>Dhātṛ</s> grant us wealth”; “<s>Dhātṛ</s> of progeny” [a fragment]; “May <s>Dhātṛ</s> grant us wealth extending eastward”; “May <s>Dhātṛ</s> grant it to the worshipper”; “May <s>Anumati</s> favor us today”; “O <s>Anumati</s>, you ...” [text corrupt]; “May she approve the winning of nourishment”; “In whom this [is placed]”; “I invoke <s>Rākā</s>”; “Those [blessings] of yours, O <s>Rākā</s>”; “O <s>Sinīvālī</s>”; “She who has fair hands”; “I invoke <s>Kuhū</s>”; and “<s>Kuhū</s> of the gods.” These are the sixteen formulas beginning with <s>Dhātṛ</s>.

children.text: imaṃ me varuṇa tattvā yāmi tvaṃ no agne sa tvaṃ no agne tvamagne ayāsyayāsanniti pañca vāruṇaṃ prajāpate na tvatprajāpatirjayānityupāṃśuyāje prājāpatye cittaṃ ca cittiścākūtaṃ cākūtiśca vijñātaṃ cāvijñānaṃ ca manaśca śakvarīśca darśaśca pūrṇamāsaśca bṛhacca rathaṃtaraṃ ca svāheti cittādi dvādaśa jayāḥ agnirbhūtānāmadhipatiḥ sa māvatvindro jyeṣṭhānāṃ yamaḥ pṛthivyā vāyurantarikṣasya sūryo divaścandramā nakṣatrāṇāṃ bṛhaspatirbrahmaṇo mitraḥ satyānāṃ varuṇo 'pāṃ samudraḥ srotyānāmannaṃ samrājyānām adhipatiṃ tanmāvatu soma oṣadhīnaṃ savitā prasavānāṃ rudraḥ paśūnāṃ tvaṣṭā rūpāṇāṃ viṣṇuḥ parvatānāṃ maruto gaṇānāmadhipatayaste māvantu pitaraḥ pitāmahāḥ pare 'vara ityaṣṭādaśāgnirbhūtādayo 'bhyātānāḥ ||
children.translated_text: “This [prayer] of mine, O <s>Varuṇa</s>,” “That [is why] I approach you,” “You, O <s>Agni</s>, [are] for us,” “So do you, O <s>Agni</s>,” and “You, O <s>Agni</s>, are <s>Ayās</s>”—these are the five <s>Vāruṇa</s> formulas. “O <s>Prajāpati</s>, none other than you” and “<s>Prajāpati</s> [wins] the victories” are used in the whispered <s>Prājāpatya</s> offering. “Consciousness and thought, intention and resolve, what is known and what is unknown, mind and <s>Śakvarī</s>, the new-moon sacrifice and the full-moon sacrifice, and the <s>Bṛhat</s> and <s>Rathantara</s>—svāhā”: these are the twelve <s>Jayā</s> formulas beginning with consciousness. “<s>Agni</s> is lord of beings; may he protect me. <s>Indra</s> is lord of the eldest; <s>Yama</s> of the earth; <s>Vāyu</s> of the atmosphere; <s>Sūrya</s> of heaven; <s>Candramas</s> of the lunar mansions; <s>Bṛhaspati</s> of sacred knowledge; <s>Mitra</s> of truths; <s>Varuṇa</s> of the waters; the ocean of the streams; and food of sovereignties—may that lord protect me. <s>Soma</s> is lord of plants; <s>Savitṛ</s> of impellings; <s>Rudra</s> of cattle; <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s> of forms; <s>Viṣṇu</s> of mountains; and the <s>Maruts</s> are lords of hosts—may they protect me. May the fathers, grandfathers, and those higher and lower protect me.” These are the eighteen <s>Abhyātāna</s> formulas beginning “<s>Agni</s> is lord of beings.”

children.text: ṛtāṣāḍṛtadhāmāgnir gandharvastasyauṣadhayo 'psarasa ūrjo nāmeti saṃhito viśvasāmā sūryo gandharvastasya marīcayo 'psarasa āyuvo nāmeti suṣumnaḥ sūryaraśmiścandramā gandharvastasya nakṣatrāṇyapsaraso bekurayo nāmeti bhujyuḥ suparṇo yajño gandharvastasya dakṣiṇā apsarasastavā nāmeti prajāpatirviśvakarmā mano gandharvas tasyarksāmāny apsaraso vahnayo nāmeti iṣiro viśvavyacā vāto gandharvastasyāpo 'psaraso mudā nāmeti bhuvanasya pata iti parameṣṭhyadhipatirmṛtyurgandharvastasya viśvamapsaraso bhuvo nāmeti sukṣitiḥ subhūtir bhadrakṛtsuvarvān parjanyo gandharvastasya vidyuto 'psaraso ruco nāmeti dūrehetiramṛḍayo mṛtyurgandharvastasya prajā apsaraso bhīruvo nāmeti cāruḥ kṛpaṇakāśī kāmo gandharvastasyādhayo 'psarasaḥ śocayantīrnāmeti sa no bhuvanasya pata iti ṛtāṣāḍṛtādi bhuvanasya sa na iti varjayitvā pratyekaṃ tābhyo 'ntā rāṣṭrabhṛto dvādarśeti prājāpatyādi mūlahomo babhūvapaitṛkayacchānte vyāhṛtiḥ ||
children.translated_text: “<s>Agni</s>, conqueror of truth and abiding in truth, is the <s>Gandharva</s>; his <s>Apsarases</s> are the herbs, called Energies. <s>Saṃhita Viśvasāman Sūrya</s> is the <s>Gandharva</s>; his <s>Apsarases</s> are the rays, called <s>Āyuvas</s>. <s>Suṣumna</s>, the sunbeam, <s>Candramas</s>, is the <s>Gandharva</s>; his <s>Apsarases</s> are the lunar mansions, called <s>Bekurayas</s>. <s>Bhujyu Suparṇa</s>, the sacrifice, is the <s>Gandharva</s>; his <s>Apsarases</s> are the sacrificial fees, called <s>Stavās</s>. <s>Prajāpati Viśvakarman</s>, the mind, is the <s>Gandharva</s>; his <s>Apsarases</s> are the <s>Ṛc</s> and <s>Sāman</s> verses, called <s>Vahnayas</s>. The impetuous, all-pervading <s>Vāyu</s> is the <s>Gandharva</s>; his <s>Apsarases</s> are the waters, called Delights. ‘O lord of the world ...’ <s>Parameṣṭhin</s>, the overlord, <s>Mṛtyu</s>, is the <s>Gandharva</s>; his <s>Apsarases</s> are the universe, called <s>Bhuvas</s>. <s>Sukṣiti</s>, <s>Subhūti</s>, <s>Bhadrakṛt</s>, and <s>Suvarvan Parjanya</s> is the <s>Gandharva</s>; his <s>Apsarases</s> are the lightning flashes, called Splendors. <s>Dūreheti Amṛḍaya Mṛtyu</s> is the <s>Gandharva</s>; his <s>Apsarases</s> are creatures, called the Timid Ones. <s>Cāru Kṛpaṇakāśin Kāma</s> is the <s>Gandharva</s>; his <s>Apsarases</s> are anxieties, called the Grieving Ones. May that lord of the world [favor] us.” These are the twelve <s>Rāṣṭrabhṛt</s> formulas, extending from “Conqueror of truth and abiding in truth” through “May that lord of the world [favor] us,” each having its corresponding ending addressed to those powers [syntax uncertain]. Beginning with the <s>Prājāpatya</s> formula, this constitutes the basic fire offering; in the ancestral rite a <s>vyāhṛti</s> (sacred utterance) is placed at the end.

children.text: athānte homamantrāḥ yadasyāgnaye sviṣṭakṛte 'gnaye 'nnādāyāgnaye 'nnapataye prajāpataya indrāya viśvebhyo devebhyaḥ sarvābhyo devatābhyaḥ sarvatraivāgnaye sviṣṭakṛte vāstupata iti sviṣṭākāro yanma ātmanaḥ punaragniścakṣuriti mindāhutī iṣṭebhya ityādi daśānte vyāhṛtirityṛddhiḥ āśrāvitaṃ brahma yadakarmeti kṛtāntaṃ yatpramatto mano jyotirayāś cāgne yadasminsvasti no yata indra iti vicchinnam adho 'syedhiṣīmahi svāhā bailvaṃ samidasi tejo 'si tejo mayi dhehi svāhā pālāśaṃ yamasya dhīmahi mṛtyorme pāhi svāhā naiyagrodhaṃ sūryasya dhīmahi cakṣurme pāhi svāhā āśvatthaṃ somasya dhīmahi cittaṃ me pāhi svāhā audumbaraṃ vāyordhīmahi prāṇānme pāhi svāhā śamīṃ brahmaṇo dhīmahi buddhiṃ me pāhi svāhā khādiramiti sapta samidhaḥ sapta te agne ṛtudhā neti pūrṇāhutī agnirbhuktam ityupajuhvāmājyaṃ gṛhītvāgnirjīrṇamiti juhvā carumavadāya hutvā samaṅtāṃ barhiriti srāvayañjuhoti tato vāmena sruvaṃ gṛhītvā dakṣiṇenājyapātraṃ saṃgṛhyāgnerupari dhārayannājyaśeṣamindrāya svāheti juhuyāt ||
children.translated_text: Next come the concluding oblation-mantras: “Whatever of this ...,” “To <s>Agni Sviṣṭakṛt</s>,” “To <s>Agni</s>, giver of food,” “To <s>Agni</s>, lord of food,” “To <s>Prajāpati</s>,” “To <s>Indra</s>,” “To all the gods,” “To every deity,” in every case “To <s>Agni Sviṣṭakṛt</s>,” and “O lord of the dwelling.” These constitute the <s>sviṣṭākāra</s> (offering that makes the sacrifice well performed). “Whatever [fault arose] from myself” and “Again <s>Agni</s> [gives] sight” are the <s>mindāhutis</s> (oblations for ritual defects). The series beginning “To those for whom sacrifice has been made” has ten formulas, with a <s>vyāhṛti</s> at the end; this is the rite for prosperity. The series from “Sacred knowledge has been proclaimed; whatever we have failed to do” to the concluding formula, and the formulas “Whatever [I did] heedlessly,” “Mind is light,” “And you, O <s>Agni</s>, are <s>Ayās</s>,” “Whatever in this,” “Well-being for us,” and “From where, O <s>Indra</s>,” are used when the rite has been interrupted. With “May we prosper beneath it, svāhā” he offers a <s>bilva</s> stick; with “You are a fuel stick, you are brilliance; place brilliance in me, svāhā,” a <s>palāśa</s> stick; with “We meditate upon <s>Yama</s>; protect me from death, svāhā,” a <s>nyagrodha</s> stick; with “We meditate upon <s>Sūrya</s>; protect my sight, svāhā,” an <s>aśvattha</s> stick; with “We meditate upon <s>Soma</s>; protect my mind, svāhā,” an <s>udumbara</s> stick; with “We meditate upon <s>Vāyu</s>; protect my vital breaths, svāhā,” a <s>śamī</s> stick; and with “We meditate upon sacred knowledge; protect my understanding, svāhā,” a <s>khadira</s> stick. These are the seven fuel sticks. With the formulas beginning “Seven for you, O <s>Agni</s>” and “According to the seasons,” he makes the full oblation. After taking ghee in the secondary ladle with “<s>Agni</s> [has consumed] what was eaten,” he portions out cooked sacrificial food with the offering ladle and offers it with “<s>Agni</s> [has digested] it.” While causing [the ghee] to stream, he offers with “May the sacrificial grass be united.” Then, taking the dipping spoon in his left hand and grasping the ghee vessel with his right, he holds them above <s>Agni</s> and offers the remaining ghee with “To <s>Indra</s>, svāhā.”

children.text: tatpātreṇādhāvamādāya sruveṇāntaritamagnistṛpyatvityupāgni paścimato vedistṛpyatviti vedyāṃ dyaustṛpyatvityākāśe pṛthivī tṛpyatviti bhūmau brahmādyāstṛpyantāmiti dakṣiṇasyāṃ tarpayati praṇītāyāṃ dakṣiṇasyāṃ daivenāpo gṛhītvauṣadhivanaspatigandharvāpsarasaścaiva tṛpyantāmityuttarasyāṃ vedyāṃ tarpayati tathottarasyāṃ praṇītāyāṃ sāpasavyam apo gṛhītvā paitṛkeṇa dakṣiṇataḥ pitaraḥ pitāmahāḥ prapitāmahāścākṣayyamastu tṛpyantāmiti dakṣiṇasyāṃ tarpayati prāsāvīr ityantaiś caturbhiḥ pravāhaṇaṃ kṛtvā dakṣiṇādipraṇidhyorupāntāṅguṣṭhānāmikābhiḥ pavitramakṣataṃ gṛhītvā pavitramasi pūrṇamasi sadasi sarvamasīti paryāyato juhotyakṣitam asīti praṇidhimuttarāṃ cālayitvā tadādhāvena prācyāṃ diśi dakṣiṇāyāṃ diśi pratīcyāṃ diśyudīcyāṃ diśyūrdhvāyāṃ diśyadhodharādharairiti yathādiśaṃ pariṣicya māhaṃ prajāmiti gṛhītvā dakṣiṇapraṇidhau svalpamādhāvaṃ srāvayitvā svāṃ yonimiti dakṣiṇapraṇidhyāṃ jalamudakapātre srāvayati āpohiṣṭhādinā tadadbhiḥ prokṣya praṇidhī visarjayati ||
children.translated_text: Taking the rinsing water with that vessel, with the offering ladle intervening, he offers satisfaction: west of the fire, saying, “May <s>Agni</s> be satisfied”; on the altar, “May the altar be satisfied”; in the sky, “May heaven be satisfied”; on the ground, “May earth be satisfied”; and on the southern side, “May <s>Brahmā</s> and the others be satisfied.” In the southern <s>praṇīta</s> vessel, having taken water with the divine manner, he offers satisfaction on the northern side of the altar, saying, “May the herbs, forest trees, <s>Gandharvas</s>, and <s>Apsarases</s> be satisfied.” Likewise, in the northern <s>praṇīta</s> vessel, wearing the sacred thread over the right shoulder and taking water in the ancestral manner, he offers satisfaction to the south, saying, “May the fathers, grandfathers, and great-grandfathers have inexhaustible benefit; may they be satisfied.” With the four formulas ending in <s>prāsāvīḥ</s>, he performs the carrying-away. From the southern deposit and the other deposits, with the tips of the thumb and ring finger, he takes the unbroken <s>pavitra</s> and offers in turn, saying, “You are a purifier; you are fullness; you are the seat; you are everything.” Saying, “You are unexhausted,” he moves the deposit and the northern one; then with that rinsing water he sprinkles in the eastern direction, the southern direction, the western direction, the northern direction, the upward direction, and downward, according to the directions, with the words ending “below and below.” Taking [water] with “May I not [harm] progeny,” he lets a little rinsing water stream into the southern deposit; with “Your own womb,” he lets the water from the southern deposit flow into the water vessel. Having sprinkled with those waters while reciting <s>āpo hi ṣṭhā</s> and the following verses, he dismisses the deposits.

children.text: punardevebhyo havyaṃ vahetyagnerdarśanena sruvaṃ visṛjya varṣiṣṭhā gahvareṣṭho 'grimiti varṣiṣṭhasamidhau juhuyād ūrdhvaṃ yajñaṃ nayatamityūrdhvasamidhau paścimataḥ paridhimapanayetyevaṃ dakṣiṇata uttarataśca paridhīn paścimato viṣṇoḥ sadanamasītyevaṃ dakṣiṇata uttarataḥ prācyāmiti ca paristaraṇabarhiṣaḥ sarvānparisamūhyāpyāyantāmiti juhoti śudhyantāṃ pitṛṣadanaṃ śudhyantāṃ devasadanamityavicchinnamāstīrya nairṛte dahedavicchinnena brahmavarcasāyeti bhūtiḥ smeti bhasma gṛhītvā lalāṭahṛdbāhukaṇṭhādīnādityaḥ somo nama ityūrdhvāgramālipyāpo hi ṣṭheti prokṣya oṃ ca me svara iti bālakṛtaṃ veti cāgniṃ pūrvavadādityaṃ copasthāya punarvedimūlamāsādyāgniṃ vaiśvānarasūktenopasthāya praṇāmaṃ kuryāditi kriyānte homaḥ oṃ ca me khara iti laukikāgnivisarjanamiti vijñāyate ||
children.translated_text: Saying, “Again carry the oblation to the gods,” and looking at the fire, he releases the ladle. He should offer on the tallest fuel-stick with “The tallest, dwelling in the cavern, foremost”; on the upward-pointing fuel-stick with “Lead the sacrifice upward.” Having removed the enclosing stick from the west, he likewise removes the enclosing sticks from the south and north. With “You are the seat of <s>Viṣṇu</s>,” and so likewise to the south, north, and east, he gathers up all the strewing grass and sacrificial grass. With “May they swell,” he offers. Spreading it unbroken, saying, “May the ancestral seat be purified; may the divine seat be purified,” he should burn it in the southwest. With “By unbroken sacred brilliance,” and saying, “You are prosperity,” he takes ash and smears it upward-pointing on the forehead, heart, arms, neck, and other places, with “<s>Āditya</s>, <s>Soma</s>, homage.” Having sprinkled with <s>āpo hi ṣṭhā</s>, and attended upon the fire as before with “Oṃ and to me the tone,” and “or what was done by a child,” he also attends upon <s>Āditya</s>. Then, returning to the base of the altar, he attends upon the fire with the <s>Vaiśvānara</s> hymn and should make obeisance. Thus at the end of the rite there is the oblation. With “Oṃ and to me the rough one,” the dismissal of an ordinary fire is understood.

children.text: Chapter 2

atha śārīreṣu saṃskāreṣvṛtusaṃgamanavarjaṃ nāndīmukhaṃ kuryāt śvaḥ kartāsmīti garbhādhānādikriyāṃ yadahaḥ karoti tadaharnandī bhavati tasyā mukhaṃ sarvadevapitṛdaivatyaṃ nāndīmukhamabhyudayaśrāddhaṃ daivikavatkaroti pūrvedyureva pūrvāhṇe yugmān brāhmaṇān suprakṣālitapāṇipādāñchrotriyān annena pariveṣyātheḍāmabhyukṣyāthāvanīdamiti maṇḍalānyupalipyāstvāsanamityāsanāni sadarbhayavāni nidhāya teṣvāsīnān puṣpādyair yathopapādam alaṃkaroti śuklabaliśvetasarṣapadadhitaṇḍulamityāmananti catuḥśuklametadādāyāgnerdakṣiṇato 'gnaye somāya prajeśāya viśvebhyo devebhya ṛṣibhyaḥ pitṛbhyo bhūtebhyaḥ sarvābhyo devatābhyo nama ityantena tannāmnā puṣpādibhirabhyarcya baliṃ dadāti ||
children.translated_text: Now, among the bodily <s>saṃskāras</s>, except for seasonal intercourse, he should perform the <s>nāndīmukha</s>. When he intends, “Tomorrow I shall perform it,” and on whatever day he performs a rite beginning with impregnation, on that day there is <s>nandī</s>; its opening, having all the gods and ancestors as its deities, is the <s>nāndīmukha</s>, the prosperity <s>śrāddha</s>, and he performs it like a rite for the gods. On the preceding day itself, in the forenoon, he feeds paired <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, learned in the Veda and with hands and feet well washed, with food. Then, after sprinkling the <s>iḍā</s>, he smears the circular places while saying <s>athāvanīdam</s>; saying “You are a seat,” he sets down seats furnished with <s>darbha</s> grass and barley. When they are seated there, he adorns them as available with flowers and the like. They teach that the white offering consists of white mustard, curds, and rice-grains; taking these four white substances, to the south of the fire he worships with flowers and the other offerings, according to the name of each, with formulas ending, “Homage to <s>Agni</s>, to <s>Soma</s>, to <s>Prajeśa</s>, to the <s>Viśve Devas</s>, to the seers, to the ancestors, to beings, to all deities,” and he gives the offering.

children.text: carumapūpādi ca nivedyodakumbhaṃ dhārāsvityadbhirāpūrya namaḥ sulomīti pāpmano 'pahatyai sapallavaṃ kūrcaṃ pavitramābharaṇaṃ tasminnidadhāti pratisarāṃ kutapasya dukūlasya vā trivṛtāṃ puṣpādyapi saṃbhṛtyādāya juhuyādṛco 'gne nayādyagnidevatyāḥ somo dhenvādi saumadaivatyā brahmajajñānādi brahmadaivatye rudramanyamityādi rudradaivatye ato devādi viṣṇudaivatyā ānoviśvādi viśvedevadaivatyā yataḥ śvamasītyādi saptarṣidaivatyā ye bhūtā ityādi bhūtadaivatyā vyāhṛtīragnaye kavyavāhanāya somāya pitṛmate yamāya cāṅgiraspataye ete ya iha pitara uśantastvā sā no dadātvityṛcaḥ pitṛdaivatyāḥ pṛthivīgatebhyaḥ pitṛbhyo 'ntarikṣagatebhyaḥ pitāmahebhyo divigatebhyaḥ prapitāmahebhyaḥ svadhā namaḥ svāheti pitṛbhyaḥ paitṛkamupavītī hutvā vyāhṛtīḥ sāmānyato devatābhyastābhyo 'ṣṭābhyo juhoti pātreṣvājyabhāgaṃ sruveṇābhighārya dvirdevaśeṣaṃ pitṛbhyaḥ prāgantaṃ kṣiptvā tadaṅguṣṭhena taccaruṃ sparśayati tato namaskṛtyā satyena rajaseti kṣīreṇa dadhnā vā śvetamannaṃ brāhmaṇānbhojayet anutthitebhyaḥ samūhyocchiṣṭaṃ śodhayitvācāntānanumānya puṇyāhaṃ vācayitvā svastisūktena tāmabhimṛśya svastidā viśaspatiriti pratisarāṃ badhnāti nāndīmukhebhyaḥ pitṛbhyaḥ svadhā namo nāndīmukhebhyaḥ pitāmahebhyaḥ svadhā namo nāndīmukhebhyaḥ prapitāmahebhyaḥ svadhā nama ityukte svadhāstviti prativadato devāntaṃ visarjayati tenodakumbhenāparedyuḥ snāyānnāndīmukhamiti vijñāyate ||
children.translated_text: After offering cooked oblation, cakes, and the like, he fills the water-pot with water while reciting <s>dhārāsu</s>. For the removal of sin, saying “Homage to <s>Sulomī</s>,” he places in it a leafy bunch, a purifier, an ornament, and a threefold protective thread made of woolen cloth or silk; having also gathered flowers and other materials, he should take them and offer. The verses beginning <s>agne naya</s> are addressed to <s>Agni</s>; those beginning <s>somo dhenvā</s> are addressed to <s>Soma</s>; those beginning <s>brahma jajñānam</s> are addressed to <s>Brahman</s>; those beginning <s>rudram anyam</s> are addressed to <s>Rudra</s>; those beginning <s>ato devāḥ</s> are addressed to <s>Viṣṇu</s>; those beginning <s>ā no viśvā</s> are addressed to the <s>Viśve Devas</s>; those beginning <s>yataḥ śvam asi</s> are addressed to the seven seers; and those beginning <s>ye bhūtāḥ</s> are addressed to beings. He offers the <s>vyāhṛtis</s> to <s>Agni Kavyavāhana</s>, to <s>Soma Pitṛmat</s>, and to <s>Yama Āṅgiraspat</s>. The verses “These fathers here,” “Desiring you,” and “May she grant us” are addressed to the ancestors. Saying “<s>Svadhā</s>, homage, <s>svāhā</s>” to the ancestors who dwell on earth, to the grandfathers who dwell in the atmosphere, and to the great-grandfathers who dwell in heaven, he offers the ancestral rite to the ancestors while wearing the sacred thread over the right shoulder. Then he offers the <s>vyāhṛtis</s> generally to the deities, and to those eight deities. In the vessels he sprinkles the ghee-portion with the <s>sruva</s>; casting the remainder for the gods twice toward the east, he makes that cooked oblation touch it with his thumb. Then, after bowing, with the verse beginning “By truth, by the realm,” he should feed the Brahmins white food with milk or curds. Before they have risen, he gathers and clears away the leavings; after they have sipped water, he obtains their approval, has the <s>puṇyāha</s> proclaimed, touches her with the <s>svasti</s> hymn, and ties the protective thread with “The giver of well-being, lord of the people.” When he has said, “<s>Svadhā</s>, homage to the nāndīmukha ancestors; <s>svadhā</s>, homage to the nāndīmukha grandfathers; <s>svadhā</s>, homage to the nāndīmukha great-grandfathers,” and they reply, “May there be <s>svadhā</s>,” he dismisses them, ending with the gods. The next day he should bathe with that water-pot. This is understood as the <s>nāndīmukha</s> rite.

children.text: atha garbhādhānādivarṣe pañcame brahmavarcasakāmamāyuṣkāmamaṣṭame navame śrīkāmaṃ vasante brāhmaṇam upanayītaikādaśe grīṣme rājanyaṃ dvādaśe śaradi vaiśyam ā ṣoḍaśādbrāhmaṇam ā dvāviṃśāt kṣatriyam ā caturviṃśādvaiśyamiti vātīte sāvitrīpatitā bhavanti teṣāmuddālakaprāyaścittaṃ dvau māsau yāvakena māsaṃ kṣīreṇāmikṣayārdhamāsamaṣṭarātraṃ ghṛtenāyācitaṃ ṣaḍrātraṃ trirātram udakenopavāsam ahorātraṃ vartata ityetaduddālakamanena vāśvamedhāvabhṛthasnānena vā vrātyastomena veṣṭvā punargarbhādhānādisaṃskārānkṛtvā śuddhā upaneyāḥ sāvitrīpatitā bhavantīti vijñāyate ||
children.translated_text: Then, counting from the year of conception and the other rites, one should initiate a Brahmin in the fifth year if he desires sacred brilliance, in the eighth if he desires long life, and in the ninth if he desires prosperity, in spring; a ruler in the eleventh year, in summer; and a Vaiśya in the twelfth year, in autumn. Alternatively, a Brahmin may be initiated up to the sixteenth year, a Kṣatriya up to the twenty-second, and a Vaiśya up to the twenty-fourth. When that time has passed, they are fallen from the <s>Sāvitrī</s>. For them the <s>Uddālaka</s> expiation is prescribed: he lives for two months on barley gruel, for one month on milk, for half a month on whey, for eight nights on ghee, for six nights on food obtained without asking, for three nights on water, and for one day and night fasting. This is the <s>Uddālaka</s>. Or, having purified him by this, or by bathing at the completion of a horse sacrifice, or by the <s>Vrātyastoma</s>, and having again performed the sacraments beginning with conception, they are purified and should be initiated. Thus it is understood that they become fallen from the <s>Sāvitrī</s>.

children.text: brāhmaṇasya pālāśo bailvo vā keśānto nirvraṇo 'numṛṣṭo 'nudvejano yūpavadavakro daṇḍaḥ kṛṣṇamṛgasyājinaṃ mauñjī mekhalā kṣatriyasya naiyagrodho lalāṭānto daṇḍo rauravamajinaṃ maurvī mekhalā vaiśyasyaudumbaro nāsikānto daṇḍo bāstavam ajinaṃ śāṇī mekhalā oṃ bhūrbhuvaḥ suvas tatsavituriti sāvitrī oṃ bhūrbhuvaḥ suvas tatsaviturāpo jyotī rasa iti prāṇāyāma oṃ bhūrbhuvaḥ suvaḥ svāheti vyāhṛtiḥ agnaye samidhamiti dve agnaye samidhāviti catvāryagnaye samidha iti samidādhānametāni brāhmaṇasya oṃ bhūrbhuvastatsavituriti sāvitrī oṃ bhūrbhuvastatsavitustejo jyotī rasa iti prāṇāyāma oṃ bhūrbhuvaḥ svāheti vyāhṛtiḥ agnaye samidhamiti dve agnaye samidhāviti samidādhānametāni kṣatriyasya oṃ bhūstatsavituriti sāvitrī oṃ bhūstatsavituragnirjyotī rasa iti prāṇāyāma oṃ bhūḥ svāheti vyāhṛtiḥ agnaye samidhamiti samidādhānametāni vaiśyasya bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: For a Brahmin the staff is of <s>palāśa</s> or <s>bilva</s> wood, reaching to the tips of the hair, free from wounds, smooth, not causing discomfort, straight like a sacrificial post; the skin is that of a black antelope, and the girdle is of muñja grass. For a Kṣatriya the staff is of <s>nyagrodha</s> wood, reaching to the forehead; the skin is that of a ruru deer, and the girdle is of bowstring hemp. For a Vaiśya the staff is of <s>udumbara</s> wood, reaching to the nose; the skin is that of a goat, and the girdle is of hemp cloth. For the Brahmin the <s>Sāvitrī</s> is “Oṃ, <s>bhūr bhuvaḥ suvaḥ</s>, that of <s>Savitṛ</s>”; the breath-control formula is “Oṃ, <s>bhūr bhuvaḥ suvaḥ</s>, that of <s>Savitṛ</s>, the waters, light, essence”; the <s>vyāhṛti</s> is “Oṃ, <s>bhūr bhuvaḥ suvaḥ</s>, <s>svāhā</s>”; and the fuel-stick placing consists of the two formulas “To <s>Agni</s> a fuel stick,” the four formulas “To <s>Agni</s> fuel sticks,” and the formula “To <s>Agni</s> a fuel stick.” These are for a Brahmin. For a Kṣatriya the <s>Sāvitrī</s> is “Oṃ, <s>bhūr bhuvaḥ</s>, that of <s>Savitṛ</s>”; the breath-control formula is “Oṃ, <s>bhūr bhuvaḥ</s>, that of <s>Savitṛ</s>, heat, light, essence”; the <s>vyāhṛti</s> is “Oṃ, <s>bhūr bhuvaḥ</s>, <s>svāhā</s>”; and the fuel-stick placing consists of the two formulas “To <s>Agni</s> a fuel stick” and the formula “To <s>Agni</s> fuel sticks.” These are for a Kṣatriya. For a Vaiśya the <s>Sāvitrī</s> is “Oṃ, <s>bhūḥ</s>, that of <s>Savitṛ</s>”; the breath-control formula is “Oṃ, <s>bhūḥ</s>, that of <s>Savitṛ</s>, <s>Agni</s>, light, essence”; the <s>vyāhṛti</s> is “Oṃ, <s>bhūḥ</s>, <s>svāhā</s>”; and the fuel-stick placing is “To <s>Agni</s> a fuel stick.” These are for a Vaiśya.

children.text: proṣṭhapadahastāv aśvinyanūrādhāpūrvottarapunarvasū mṛgaśiro vā yāvanti puṃnāmāni nakṣatrāṇi tatrāgner vāyavyām upavītājinamekhalāhatavastradaṇḍaśarāvāśmasamiddarbhādisambhārān darbheṣu saṃbhṛtya saṃ ca tve jagmuriti prokṣayatyathājyenāghāraṃ hutvācāntaṃ maṅgalayuktaṃ kumāramāsayitvāgnernairṛtyāṃ mastake darbhau prāguttarāgrau vinyasya saromāṇaṃ darbhamindra śastramiti caturbhiḥ pradakṣiṇaṃ caturdiśaṃ chittvā yenāvapadyatkṣureṇeti sarvato vapati nādho jatrorgośakṛdyukte śarāve keśāngṛhṇīyāt yatra mauṇḍyaṃ śikhābhrūvarjam ā nakhaṃ vapati snātvācāntaṃ puṇyāhaṃ vācayitvā bhuktavantam āsayati dakṣiṇe kumāramatha paristīryāyurdā agna āyurdā deveti pradhānaṃ pañca vāruṇaṃ vyāhṛtiparyantaṃ juhotyātiṣṭheti vāyavyām aśma pādāṅguṣṭhena dakṣiṇena sparśayati yā akṛntanniti vastramiyam duruktāditi mekhalāṃ parīdamityuttarīyaṃ yajñopavītamityupavītaṃ mitrasya cakṣuriti kṛṣṇājinaṃ tasmai dadāti ||
children.translated_text: On the lunar mansions <s>Proṣṭhapada</s>, <s>Hasta</s>, <s>Aśvinī</s>, <s>Anūrādhā</s>, <s>Pūrvottarā</s>, <s>Punarvasū</s>, <s>Mṛgaśiras</s>, or on whatever lunar mansions have masculine names, he gathers on <s>darbha</s> grass, to the northwest of the fire, the materials: sacred thread, antelope skin, girdle, unworn garment, staff, bowl, stone, fuel sticks, <s>darbha</s> grass, and the rest. With the formula <s>saṃ ca tve jagmuḥ</s> he sprinkles them. Then, having offered an <s>āghāra</s> with clarified butter, he seats the boy, who has sipped water and is furnished with auspicious marks. To the southwest of the fire he places two blades of <s>darbha</s> on his head, with their tips toward the east and north. With the four formulas beginning <s>indra śastram</s> he cuts a hairy blade of <s>darbha</s> clockwise in the four directions, and with <s>yenāvapadyat kṣureṇa</s> he shaves him all around, not below the collarbone. He should collect the hair in a bowl mixed with cow dung. Where complete shaving is prescribed, he shaves everything down to the nails except the topknot and eyebrows. After the boy has bathed and sipped water, he has the auspicious-day proclamation made, and seats him after he has eaten, on his right side. Then, having spread the grass around the fire, he offers the principal oblation with <s>āyurdā agna</s> and <s>āyurdā deva</s>, and five <s>Vāruṇa</s> formulas ending with the <s>vyāhṛtis</s>. With <s>ātiṣṭha</s> he makes him touch a stone in the northwest with the big toe of his right foot. With <s>yā akṛntan</s> he gives the garment; with <s>iyam duruktāt</s>, the girdle; with <s>parīdam</s>, the upper garment; with <s>yajñopavītam</s>, the sacred thread; and with <s>mitrasya cakṣuḥ</s>, the black antelope skin.

children.text: tato vidhivadācamanaṃ kārayitvā sadasyānanujñāpya devasya tveti bāhū ālabhyottare prāṅmukhaḥ prāṅmukham upanayītāyuṣṭe viśvata iti dakṣiṇapāṇiṃ gṛhītvoddharaty agniṣṭe hastam agrabhīditi visarjaty asāv apo 'śānety ācāraṃ mama hṛdaya iti tasya hṛdayasparśanaṃ kṛtvā bhūrbhuvaḥ suvaḥ suprajā iti praśaṃsati bhūr ṛkṣu tveti bhuvo yajuḥṣu tveti suvaḥ sāmasu tvetīṣṭutasta ityanalasya ta itīdaṃ vatsyāva iti ṣaḍbhiḥ karṇe japitvā nāma śarmāntaṃ kuryādagnirāyuṣmānityādikaiḥ pañcabhirdakṣiṇahaste kaniṣṭhādyaṅgulyagrāṇi paryāyeṇa visṛjed āyurdā iti dakṣiṇe karṇe pratiṣṭha vāyāviti vāme ca japati svasti devetyagniṃ pradakṣiṇaṃ kārayitvā dakṣiṇe niveśya rāṣṭrabhṛdasīti kūrcaṃ dattvā śaṃ no devīriti prokṣya mūlahomaṃ vyāhṛtiparyantaṃ juhotyaditiste kakṣyāmiti hutaśeṣaṃ bhojayitvā yoge yoge tavastaram ityācamanaṃ dadāti śataminnv ityādityaṃ namaskṛtyāgantrā samaganmahīti pradakṣiṇaṃ kārayitvā śakāya tvetyuttamāṅgamabhimṛśyādhīhi bho iti tena prārthito gururathāha sāvitrīṃ bho iti śiṣyamanuśāsti gaṇānāṃ tveti gaṇamukhyamojo 'sīti sāvitrīṃ pāvakā naḥ sarasvatīti sarasvatīṃ ca praṇamya yathoktaṃ sāvitrīṃ paccho 'rdharcaśo vyastāṃ samastāmadhyāpayet ||
children.translated_text: Then, after having him sip water according to rule and asking permission of the assembly, the initiator touches his arms with <s>devasya tvā</s> and, facing east on the northern side, initiates him while the boy also faces east. Taking his right hand with <s>āyuṣ ṭe viśvataḥ</s>, he raises him; with <s>agniṣ ṭe hastam agrabhīt</s> he releases him. With <s>asāv apo 'śāna</s> he teaches the proper conduct. Having touched his heart with <s>mama hṛdaye</s>, he praises him with <s>bhūr bhuvaḥ suvaḥ suprajāḥ</s>. He whispers six formulas into his ear: <s>bhūr ṛkṣu tvā</s>, <s>bhuvo yajuḥṣu tvā</s>, <s>suvaḥ sāmasu tvā</s>, <s>iṣṭutas te</s>, <s>analasya te</s>, and <s>idaṃ vatsyāva</s>. He should give him a name ending in <s>śarman</s>. With the five formulas beginning <s>agnir āyuṣmān</s> he releases, in sequence, the tips of the fingers of the right hand, beginning with the little finger. In his right ear he whispers <s>āyurdā</s>, and in the left <s>pratiṣṭha vāyau</s>. With <s>svasti deve</s> he has him go clockwise around the fire, seats him on the right, gives him a brush of grass with <s>rāṣṭrabhṛd asi</s>, sprinkles him with <s>śaṃ no devīḥ</s>, and offers the basic oblation ending with the <s>vyāhṛtis</s>. With <s>aditis te kakṣyām</s> he feeds him what remains of the oblation, and with <s>yoge yoge tavastaram</s> he gives him water for sipping. Having bowed to <s>Āditya</s> with <s>śatam in nu</s>, and having made him go clockwise with <s>āgantrā samaganmahi</s>, he touches the crown of his head with <s>śakāya tvā</s>. When the student has requested him, saying, 'Teach me, sir,' the teacher then says, 'The <s>Sāvitrī</s>, sir,' and instructs the pupil. After bowing to the chief of groups with <s>gaṇānāṃ tvā</s>, to the <s>Sāvitrī</s> with <s>ojo 'si</s>, and to <s>Sarasvatī</s> with <s>pāvakā naḥ sarasvatī</s>, he should teach the <s>Sāvitrī</s> as prescribed: by quarter, by half-verse, divided, and complete.

children.text: dhātādipūrvaṃ savitre kāṇḍarṣaye sadasaspatim ā devo yātvabhīvṛtaṃ sa ghā no vi janāñchyāvā vi suparṇo bhagaṃ dhiyamiti sāvitravratasūktamagne vāyavindrāditya vratānāmiti sāvitravratabandhaṃ pañcabhirvyāhṛtyantaṃ juhotyagnaye samidhamiti dve agnaye samidhāviti catvāryagnaye samidha iti sapta pālāśāṅkurāṇi ghṛtāktāni juhoti sūrya eṣa te putra ityādityaṃ darśayatyaṣṭābhiḥ samidbhir homakarmaṇi śiṣyaṃ yojayedyathā heti dakṣiṇādipradakṣiṇaṃ vediṃ parimṛjya pūrvavatparistṛṇāti vyāhṛtīreṣā te medhāṃ ma indro dadātv apsarāsv ā māṃ medhetyaṣṭau juhoti yathā heti tathā parimṛjya prāsāvīrityantaiś caturbhiḥ pravāhaṇaṃ kṛtvā bhūtiḥ smeti bhasmālipyāpo hi ṣṭheti prokṣya yatte agne tejastenetyagnim ud vayam ityādityaṃ copatiṣṭheta nityaṃ sāyaṃprātarevaṃ juhuyādyato brahmadattam idam ijyam agnihotram etanmūlāstadagnaya iti brahmavādino vadanti ||
children.translated_text: With the formulas beginning with <s>Dhātṛ</s> and preceding <s>Savitṛ</s>, with <s>sadasaspatim</s>, <s>ā devo yātu abhīvṛtam</s>, <s>sa ghā no vi janān</s>, <s>śyāvā vi</s>, <s>suparṇo</s>, and <s>bhagaṃ dhiyam</s>, he recites the <s>Sāvitravrata</s> hymn. With <s>agne vāyav indrāditya vratānām</s> and five formulas ending with the <s>vyāhṛtis</s>, he performs the binding of the <s>Sāvitrī</s> vow. With <s>agnaye samidham</s>, two formulas; with <s>agnaye samidhau</s>, four; and with <s>agnaye samidhaḥ</s>, seven, he offers shoots of <s>palāśa</s> smeared with ghee. With <s>sūrya eṣa te putraḥ</s> he shows him <s>Āditya</s>. He should employ the student in the fire rite with eight fuel sticks. Having wiped the altar clockwise beginning on the south with <s>yathā ha</s>, he spreads the grass around it as before. He offers the eight formulas: the <s>vyāhṛtis</s>, <s>eṣā te medhā</s>, <s>mā indro dadātu</s>, <s>apsarāsu</s>, and <s>ā māṃ medhā</s>. Having wiped in the same way with <s>yathā ha</s>, he performs the carrying forward with the four formulas ending in <s>prāsāvīḥ</s>. With <s>bhūtiḥ sme</s> he smears on ashes; with <s>āpo hi ṣṭhā</s> he sprinkles. With <s>yat te agne tejas tena</s> he attends upon <s>Agni</s>, and with <s>ud vayam</s> upon <s>Āditya</s>. In this way he should offer daily, both evening and morning. For the expounders of sacred knowledge say: since this sacrificial act is given by <s>Brahman</s>, it is the <s>Agnihotra</s>, and those fires have this as their root.

children.text: agniṣṭa āyuriti daṇḍamindro marudbhiriti śarāvaṃ kaṭhinaṃ vā bhaikṣapātraṃ dadyāt bhavati bhikṣāṃ dehīti brāhmaṇo brūyātkṣatriyo bhikṣāṃ bhavati dehīti vaiśyo bhikṣāṃ dehi bhavatīti maunavratena brāhmaṇebhyo bhaikṣamāmam itarebhyo gṛhṇīyād yasya ta iti gurur bhaikṣam ādāya suśrava iti prokṣayati haviṣāpūpalājasamāyutena mindāhutī hutvāntahomo hūyate maunavratenā saṃdhyāgamāttiṣṭhati tasmā āśramadharmāṇyācakṣīta coditātikrame daṇḍena na hanyādduṣṭavākyairna śapatyatikramānurūpaṃ kṛcchramādiśati guruṇā śiṣyo rakṣitavyo yasmācchiṣyakṛtaṃ duritaṃ prāpnotyavaśyamakurvantaṃ śiṣyaṃ tyajatyanyathā tyāge patnīputraśiṣyāṇāṃ patati kāṣāyājinayoranyataravāsā jaṭī śikhī vā mekhalī daṇḍī sūtrājinadhārī brahmacārī śucirakṣāralavaṇāśī yathokteṣu varṇeṣu brahmacāridharmāṇyanutiṣṭhatīti vijñāyate ||
children.translated_text: With “<s>Agniṣṭa</s> is life” he should give the staff, and with “<s>Indra</s> with the <s>Maruts</s>” a dish, or a hard begging bowl. A <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> should say, “Lady, give alms”; a <s>Kṣatriya</s>, “Give alms, lady”; a <s>Vaiśya</s>, “Give alms, O lady.” Observing a vow of silence, he should take raw alms from <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> and from others. Taking the alms with the formula “That which is yours,” the teacher sprinkles it with “Good fame.” Having offered the <s>mindāhutis</s> (oblations for defects) together with an oblation of cakes and parched grain, the final oblation is offered. Observing a vow of silence, he stands until the coming of twilight. The teacher should explain to him the duties of the life-stage. When he transgresses an injunction, he should not strike him with the staff, nor curse him with harsh words, but should prescribe a <s>kṛcchra</s> or similar penance according to the transgression. The pupil must be protected by the teacher, because the teacher necessarily incurs the sin committed by the pupil. If the pupil does not act as he should, the teacher abandons him; otherwise, by abandoning a wife, son, or pupil, he falls. Wearing either ochre cloth or an antelope skin, wearing matted hair or a topknot, girdled, staff-bearing, wearing the sacred thread and antelope skin, the brahmacārin is pure, eats food without alkali or salt, and observes the brahmacārin's duties according to the stated social classes. So it is understood.

children.text: atha pārāyaṇavratāni caturthe pañcame saptame vā puṇye puṃnāmni nakṣatre śiṣyam ācāntaṃ puṇyāhaṃ vācayitvāgniṃ paristīrya prāṅmukham upaveśayati tasyottare mātā brahmacārī vāsīta dhātādipūrvaṃ sāvitravratasūktam agne vāyavindrāditya vratānām ityūhitvācāriṣaṃ visarjayāmīti sāvitravratavisargaṃ hutvā pūrvāṇi sūtradaṇḍādīny apsu visṛjya snātāya navānyupavītādīni pūrvavad dattvā tam adbhir abhyukṣya dakṣiṇe niveśya dhātādipūrvaṃ prajāpataye kāṇḍarṣaye sadasaspatiṃ prajāpate na tvadrayīṇāṃ patiṃ prajāpate tvaṃ nidhipās taveme lokāḥ prajāpatiṃ prathamaṃ yo rāya ityagnyādiṣu pañcasu prājāpatyam ityubhayatrohitvā vārṣikaṃ prājāpatyavratabandhaṃ hutvā śiṣyeṇa vrataṃ bandhayati varṣe varṣe tathaiva vratavisargaṃ hutvā tat tad vrataṃ visṛjyānyadvrataṃ badhnāti ||
children.translated_text: Now the pārāyaṇa vows.
