On an auspicious lunar mansion with a male name, in the fourth, fifth, or seventh year, after the pupil has sipped water and after he has had the auspicious-day rite proclaimed, the teacher spreads the fire and seats him facing east. To his north the mother or a brahmacārin should sit. With the formula beginning with <s>Dhātṛ</s>, adapting the Sāvitra-vow hymn with “O <s>Agni</s>, O <s>Vāyu</s>, O <s>Indra</s>, O <s>Āditya</s>, of the vows,” and saying “I have practiced; I release,” he offers the release of the Sāvitra vow. Having cast the former thread, staff, and other articles into water, and having given new sacred threads and the other articles as before to the bathed pupil, he sprinkles him with water and seats him on the southern side. With the formula beginning with <s>Dhātṛ</s>, for <s>Prajāpati</s>, the seer of the book-section, he adapts, in both places, “<s>Sadasaspati</s>,” “O <s>Prajāpati</s>,” “Not from you,” “Lord of riches,” “O <s>Prajāpati</s>, you are guardian of treasures,” “These worlds are yours,” and “<s>Prajāpati</s> first, who for wealth,” and, among the five beginning with <s>Agni</s>, the Prājāpatya hymn. Having offered the annual binding of the Prājāpatya vow, he binds the pupil with the vow. Year by year, after offering the release of the vow in the same way, he releases that particular vow and binds another vow.

children.text: somāya kāṇḍarṣaye sadasaspatiṃ somo dhenumaṣāḍhaṃ tvaṃ soma kratubhiryā te dhāmāni haviṣā tvamimā oṣadhīryā te dhāmāni divīti sūktaṃ saumyavratasyāgnaye kāṇḍarṣaye sadasaspatimagne naya pra vaḥ śukrāyācchā giro 'gne tvamasmadagne tvaṃ pāraya pra kāravo mananeti sūktamāgneyavratasya viśvebhyo devebhyaḥ kāṇḍarṣaye sadasaspatim ā no viśve śaṃ no devā ye savituragne yāhi dyauḥ pitarviśve devāḥ śṛṇuteti sūktaṃ vaiśvadevavratasya brahmaṇe kāṇḍarṣaye sadasaspatiṃ brahma jajñānaṃ pitā virājāṃ brahma devānantarasmin brahman devāś catasra iti sūktaṃ brāhmavratasya ṛtaṃ ca satyaṃ ca devakṛtasya yanme gabha taratsa mandīti prājāpatye vasoḥ pavitraṃ pavasva viśvacarṣaṇa iti saumye jātavedasa ityāgneye viṣṇornu kaṃ sahasraśīrṣā tvamagne rudrā tvāhārṣamiti vaiśvadeve ekākṣaraṃ tvakṣariteti brāhme tattadvratadaivatyaṃ svādhyāyasūktaṃ tattatkāṇḍaṃ cādhīyīta ||
children.translated_text: For the Saumya vow, the hymn is addressed to <s>Soma</s>, the seer of the book-section: “<s>Sadasaspati</s>,” “<s>Soma</s> the cow,” “The unassailable one,” “You, O <s>Soma</s>, with rites,” “Those abodes of yours,” “With oblation,” “You these herbs,” and “Those abodes of yours in heaven.” For the Āgneya vow, the hymn is addressed to <s>Agni</s>, the seer of the book-section: “<s>Sadasaspati</s>,” “O <s>Agni</s>, lead,” “Forward to you bright songs,” “O <s>Agni</s>, you from us,” “O <s>Agni</s>, you carry across,” “Forward, singers,” and “With the mind.” For the Vaiśvadeva vow, the hymn is addressed to the <s>Viśve Devas</s>, the seer of the book-section: “<s>Sadasaspati</s>,” “To us, all [gods],” “Blessing for us, O gods,” “Those of <s>Savitṛ</s>,” “O <s>Agni</s>, come,” “Heaven, O father,” and “All gods, hear.” For the Brāhma vow, the hymn is addressed to <s>Brahman</s>, the seer of the book-section: “<s>Sadasaspati</s>,” “<s>Brahman</s> was born,” “Father of the shining ones,” “<s>Brahman</s> among the gods,” and “In <s>Brahman</s> the gods, the four.” The private-recitation hymn belonging to each vow-deity should be studied: in the Prājāpatya, “Truth and reality” and “What was made by the gods,” “What in my womb,” and “He crossed, he exhilarates”; in the Saumya, “Purifier of <s>Vasu</s>, purify yourself, O all-seeing one”; in the Āgneya, “For <s>Jātavedas</s>”; in the Vaiśvadeva, “Now of <s>Viṣṇu</s>,” “Thousand-headed,” “You, O <s>Agni</s>,” “O <s>Rudra</s>,” and “I have brought you”; and in the Brāhma, “The single syllable” and “You are imperishable.” He should also study the corresponding book-section.

children.text: tathaiva dhātādivratavisargaṃ hutvā brāhmavrataṃ visṛjya navānyupavītādīni pūrvavaddattvā pravargyadevatābhyaḥ kalpayāmi sāṃrājyai kalpayāmi mahāvīrāya kalpayāmi pṛthivyai kalpayāmi svāhetyuttare somāya kalpayāmi pitṛbhyaḥ kalpayāmi pitṛbhyo mantrapatibhyaḥ kalpayāmi rudrāya kalpayāmi rudrāya rudrahotre kalpayāmi svāheti dakṣiṇe cāhutīretā hutvāgne vratapate śukriyavrataṃ bandhayāmīti śukriyavrataṃ ṣāṇmāsikaṃ traimāsikaṃ vā badhnīyāccitaḥ stha paricitaḥ sthetyādinānuvākena śiro 'hatena vāsasāveṣṭayedyathainamahaḥ sūryo nābhitapenmukham asya tasmād rephāyati strīśūdrābhyām anabhibhāṣya śukriyabrāhmaṇāruṇanārāyaṇādyāraṇyakāṇḍam adhīyīta iti vratapārāyaṇaṃ vijñāyate ||
children.translated_text: In the same way, after offering the release of the vow beginning with <s>Dhātṛ</s>, after releasing the Brāhma vow, and after giving new sacred threads and the other articles as before, he offers these oblations to the Pravargya deities: “I prepare for [the deity of] sovereignty; I prepare for sovereignty; I prepare for <s>Mahāvīra</s>; I prepare for the earth; svāhā” on the northern side; and “I prepare for <s>Soma</s>; I prepare for the ancestors; I prepare for the ancestral lords of mantras; I prepare for <s>Rudra</s>; I prepare for <s>Rudra</s> the Rudra-hotṛ; svāhā” on the southern side. Having offered these oblations, he should bind the Śukriya vow, for six months or for three months, saying, “O <s>Agni</s>, lord of vows, I bind the Śukriya vow.” With the anuvāka beginning “You are piled up; you are heaped around,” he should wrap the head in an unworn garment, so that the sun may not burn his face by day; because of that his face becomes radiant. Without conversing with women or <s>Śūdras</s>, he should study the Śukriya Brāhmaṇa, the Āruṇa, the Nārāyaṇa, and the other forest-book sections. Thus the pārāyaṇa of the vows is understood.

children.text: athāṣāḍhopākarma kuryād āpūryamāṇapakṣe riktāparvaṇī varjayitvā budhavāre tithiṃ gṛhṇāti tatrāghāraṃ hutvāgniṃ paristīrya śiṣyaṃ vāpayitvā snātaṃ puṇyāhaṃ vācayitvā prokṣaṇaiḥ prokṣyāgniṃ pradakṣiṇaṃ kārayitvā kūrcaṃ dadāty āsayitvā dakṣiṇe śaṃ no devīriti prokṣya pradhānāḥ pañcāśadāhutīr ājyacarubhyām akṣatadhānābhyāṃ vā juhotyagnaye pṛthivyai ṛgvedāya yajurvedāya sāmavedāyātharvaṇavedāya vāyave 'ntarikṣāya divasāya sūryāya digbhyaś candramase 'dhyāyāyānadhyāyāyādhyāyadevatāyā anadhyāyadevatāyai śraddhāyai medhāyai dhāraṇāyā ācāryāya chandasa ṛṣibhyaḥ saptarṣibhyo munibhyo gurubhyo 'horātrebhyo 'rdhamāsebhyo māsebhya ṛtubhyaḥ saṃvatsarebhyaḥ parivatsarebhya idāvatsarebhya idvatsarebhyo vatsarebhyo brahmaṇe sāvitryai prajāpataya uśanase cyavanāya bṛhaspataye somāyāṅgirase darbhāya śaṅkhāya likhitāya sthūlaśirase vainateyāya śikhina īśvarāyādhikṛtādhidevatābhyaḥ sadasaspatimadbhutaṃ priyamindrasya kāmyam saniṃ medhāmayāsiṣaṃ svāheti pūrvavat prājāpatyavratabandhaṃ dhātādi pañca vāruṇaṃ mūlahomaṃ sviṣṭākāraṃ ca hutvā hutaśeṣam aditiste kakṣyāmiti bhojayitvā yoge yoge tavastaram ityācamanaṃ dadāty atha prāṅmukhamudaṅmukhaṃ vā brahmāñjaliṃ kārayitvā dakṣiṇam adhyāsīnaṃ vedānvedau vedaṃ vā sūtrasahitam adhyāpayatyantarāpyevam adhyāpayitukāmo hutvādhyāpayed ardhapañcamānardhaṣaṣṭhān vā māsān adhyāyānupākurvītāta ūrdhvaṃ śukleṣu kāmaṃ tu vedāṅgānīti vedopākaraṇam atha śrāvaṇe paurṇamāsyāmagniṃ paristīrya śiṣyaṃ vāpayitvā snātaṃ puṇyāhaṃ vācayitvā pūrvavadvratabandhaṃ dhātādi pañca vāruṇaṃ mūlahomaṃ sviṣṭākāraṃ ca juhotyadhyayanapārāyaṇāyeti śrāvaṇaṃ tathaiva naiṣṭhiko yāvajjīvam āśramadharmāṇyanu tiṣṭhetopākurvāṇo vedamadhītya snāyāditi vijñāyate ||
children.translated_text: Now he should perform the Āṣāḍha <s>upākarman</s> (commencement of Vedic study) in the waxing fortnight, avoiding an empty lunar day and the full- or new-moon day, taking a lunar day that falls on a Wednesday. There, after offering the <s>āghāra</s>, spreading grass around the fire, having the pupil shaved, bathed, and the auspicious-day rite proclaimed, sprinkling him with the sprinklings, making him circumambulate the fire clockwise, giving him a brush of grass, seating him on the southern side, and sprinkling him with <s>śaṃ no devīḥ</s>, he offers the principal fifty oblations, with ghee and cooked oblation, or with unbroken rice and grain: to <s>Agni</s>, Earth, the <s>Ṛgveda</s>, the <s>Yajurveda</s>, the <s>Sāmaveda</s>, the <s>Atharvaveda</s>, <s>Vāyu</s>, the atmosphere, heaven, the Sun, the directions, the Moon, study, non-study, the deity of study, the deity of non-study, faith, intelligence, retention, the teacher, the metres, the seers, the seven seers, the sages, the gurus, the days and nights, the half-months, the months, the seasons, the years, the parivatsaras, the idāvatsaras, the idvatsaras, the vatsaras, <s>Brahman</s>, <s>Sāvitrī</s>, <s>Prajāpati</s>, <s>Uśanas</s>, <s>Cyavana</s>, <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, <s>Soma</s>, <s>Aṅgiras</s>, <s>Darbha</s>, <s>Śaṅkha</s>, <s>Likhita</s>, <s>Sthūlaśiras</s>, <s>Vainateya</s>, <s>Śikhin</s>, <s>Īśvara</s>, and the presiding deities in charge, with the formula ending, ‘I have obtained the wondrous lord of the assembly, dear to <s>Indra</s>, desirable, rich in intelligence; svāhā.’ As before, after offering the binding of the Prājāpatya vow, the five oblations beginning with <s>Dhātṛ</s>, the Vāruṇa oblations, the basic oblation, and the <s>sviṣṭakṛt</s>, he feeds him the remains of the oblation with <s>aditis te kakṣyām</s> and gives him water for sipping with <s>yoge yoge tavastaram</s>. Then, having made him face east or north and form the Brahman-handful gesture, seated on the right, he teaches him the Vedas, two Vedas, or one Veda together with the sūtra. Even in the middle of the term, if he wishes to teach in this way, he should offer and teach. For four and a half or five and a half months he should undertake the periods of study; after that, during the bright fortnights he may study the ancillary sciences at will. This is the Vedic <s>upākaraṇa</s>. Then, on the full-moon day of Śrāvaṇa, after spreading grass around the fire, having the pupil shaved and bathed, and having the auspicious-day rite proclaimed, he offers as before the vow-binding, the five oblations beginning with <s>Dhātṛ</s>, the Vāruṇa oblations, the basic oblation, and the <s>sviṣṭakṛt</s>, saying, ‘For the completion of study.’ This is the Śrāvaṇa rite. Likewise, one who is a lifelong student should observe the duties of the life-stage for as long as he lives; one who is undertaking the vow should bathe after studying the Veda. So it is understood.

children.text: atha samāvartanaṃ vyākhyāsyāma udagayana āpūryamāṇapakṣe tiṣyottareṣu citrāviśākhayorhastarohiṇyormṛgaśirasi vā nakṣatre yatrāpastatrāgāre goṣṭhe vāghāraṃ hutvāgniṃ paristīrya tathaiva dhātādivratavisargaṃ hutvā vayaḥ suparṇā iti vastrāvakuṇṭhanaṃ mocayitvā śukriyavrataṃ visṛjatīmaṃ stomaṃ tryāyuṣaṃ jamadagneriti pradhānaṃ pañca vāruṇaṃ mūlahomāntaṃ hutvodvayaṃ tamasa udu tyam ityetābhyām ādityam upasthāyoduttamam ityuttarīyam athā vayamiti sūtradaṇḍādīny apsu visṛjya śivo nāmāsīti kṣuramupalena karṣayitvā sākṣatair ādhāvaiḥ śivā na iti śiro 'ñjayitvā godānam apa undantvoṣadhe trāyasva yatkṣureṇeti caturdiśaṃ yenāvapaditi sarvato nakhāntaṃ vapati śarāve sānaḍuhagośakṛti keśādīnyādāyedamahamamuṣyetyudumbaradarbhayormūle goṣṭhe vā gūhayedannādyāya vyūhadhvamiti dantadhāvanamaudumbareṇa kāṣṭhena karoti śītoṣṇābhiradbhirāpo hi ṣṭhetyādibhir ṛgbhis tisṛbhiḥ snāpayitvā hiraṇyapavamānābhyāṃ prokṣayatīti pūrvaṃ tathā pradhānānhutvā purodayādādityasya brāhmavrataṃ visṛjya śukriyavratasya grahaṇavisargāvityeke ||
children.translated_text: Now we shall explain the <s>samāvartana</s> (return home after studentship). During the sun's northern course, in the waxing fortnight, under the lunar mansions <s>Tiṣya</s>, <s>Uttarā</s>, <s>Citrā</s>, <s>Viśākhā</s>, <s>Hasta</s>, <s>Rohiṇī</s>, or <s>Mṛgaśiras</s>, wherever there is water, in a house or a cow-pen, after offering the <s>āghāra</s>, spreading grass around the fire, and in the same way offering the release of the vow beginning with <s>Dhātṛ</s>, he loosens the wrapping garment with <s>vayaḥ suparṇāḥ</s> and releases the Śukriya vow. Having offered the principal oblation with <s>imaṃ stomam</s> and <s>tryāyuṣaṃ jamadagneḥ</s>, the five Vāruṇa oblations, and the basic oblation up to its end, he attends upon <s>Āditya</s> with the two formulas <s>ud vayaṃ tamasaḥ</s> and <s>ud u tyam</s>. With <s>ud uttamam</s> he takes the upper garment. Then with <s>athā vayam</s> he casts the thread, staff, and the rest into water. Saying <s>śivo nāmāsi</s>, he rubs the razor on a stone; with unhusked grains and washing waters, saying <s>śivā naḥ</s>, he anoints the head. The gift of a cow is made. With <s>āpa undantu</s>, <s>oṣadhe trāyasva</s>, and <s>yat kṣureṇa</s>, in the four directions, and with <s>yenāvapat</s>, he shaves him all around down to the tips of the nails. Placing the hair and the rest in a dish with cow dung from a cow with calf, he should conceal it with <s>idam aham amuṣya</s> at the roots of an udumbara tree and darbha grass, or in a cow-pen. Saying <s>annādyāya vyūhadhvam</s>, he cleans his teeth with a stick of udumbara wood. Having bathed him with cool and warm waters, using the three verses beginning <s>āpo hi ṣṭhā</s>, he sprinkles him with the two verses of the gold-purifying hymn. Then, as before, after offering the principal oblations, he releases the Brāhma vow before sunrise. Some say that the taking and release of the Śukriya vow are performed likewise.

children.text: divi śrayasvetyahate vāsasī gandhābharaṇādīni ca prokṣya namo grahāyeti gandhaṃ gṛhītvā prācīnamañjaliṃ kṛtvāpsarassviti gātrāṇyanulepayet tejovatsava iti vastraṃ paridhāya somasya tanūrasītyuttarīyaṃ gṛhṇāti pūrvavanmekhalādīnyādadītābharaṇakuṇḍalamaṇīnbadareṇa suvarṇena vā kṛtānācchādya darbheṇa badhnīyāt ||
children.translated_text: With <s>divi śrayasva</s>, he sprinkles unworn garments, perfumes, ornaments, and the rest. Taking perfume with <s>namo grahāya</s>, he forms his joined hands facing east and, with <s>apsarassu</s>, anoints his limbs. With <s>tejovatsavaḥ</s> he puts on the garment, and with <s>somasya tanūr asi</s> he takes the upper garment. As before, he should take up the girdle and the other articles. Having covered the ornaments, earrings, and jewels, made of badara wood or of gold, he should fasten them with darbha grass.

children.text: tadagnāvupari dhārayannāyuṣyaṃ varcasyamuccairvādi śunamahaṃ priyaṃ meyamoṣadhīti pañcabhirjuhuyātsamrājaṃ ca virājaṃ cetyudakapātre pariplāvya ṛtubhiriṣṭvārtavairiyamoṣadhīti tābhyāṃ kuṇḍalābhyāṃ dakṣiṇādikarṇayoralaṃkaroti śubhika iti maṇinā kaṇṭhamāmucyedaṃ brahma punīmaha ityaṅgulīyakaṃ gṛhītvā yadāñjanamiti dakṣiṇaṃ cakṣuryanme mana iti vāmaṃ cāñjanenāñjayitvemāḥ sumanasa iti srajamādāya devasya tvetyādarśamavekṣeta tenaiva vaiṇavaṃ daṇḍamṛjuṃ gṛhṇīyād indrasya vajro 'sīti vegavejam iti trir unmārṣṭyupānahāvityupānahāvāruhya prajāpateḥ śaraṇaṃ bhuvaḥ punātviti dvābhyāṃ chattraṃ gṛhṇīyādyo me daṇḍa iti punardaṇḍaṃ pramāde satyāharettato vāhanaṃ pūjayitvā pratiṣṭhe stho devatānāmityabhimṛśya rathaṃtaramasīti rathamaśvo 'si hayo 'sītyaśvam indrasya tvā vajreṇeti hastinam āruhyāvatared abhyāgatam uttamaṃ kanyāpradaḥ saṃ sravantviti nirīkṣya yaśo 'sītyāvasathe viṣṭaraṃ kūrcaṃ pādyamarghyamācamanīyaṃ madhuparkaṃ ca saṃkalpayati ||
children.translated_text: Holding that over the fire, he should offer five oblations with the formulas beginning “Life-giving, increasing sacred brilliance, speaking aloud,” and “I am dear; may this plant be dear to me.” Placing the two earrings in the water-vessel with “Imperial and sovereign,” and having sacrificed with the seasonal formulas, he adorns the right and then the other ear with those earrings, saying “This plant.” With “Auspicious” he fastens a jewel on the neck. Taking a ring with “This sacred power we purify,” he anoints the right eye with collyrium using “That collyrium,” and the left with “That which is my mind.” Taking a garland with “These fair flowers,” he should look in a mirror with “Of the god.” With that same formula he takes a straight staff of bilva wood; saying “You are <s>Indra</s>’s thunderbolt,” and “Swift-moving,” he wipes it three times. Saying “Sandals,” he mounts the sandals. With the two formulas “You are the refuge of <s>Prajāpati</s>” and “May the earth purify,” he takes an umbrella. If the staff is lost through carelessness, he should retrieve it again with “The staff that is mine.” Then, after worshiping the vehicle, he touches it with “You two are the support of the gods”: the chariot with “You are the <s>Rathantara</s>,” the horse with “You are a horse, you are a steed,” and the elephant with “With <s>Indra</s>’s thunderbolt”; having mounted, he descends. When the excellent guest has arrived, the giver of the maiden looks at him with “May they flow together,” and, saying “You are fame,” prepares at the lodging a seat, a grass seat, water for the feet, an arghya offering, water for sipping, and a madhuparka.

children.text: tatropaveśya rāṣṭrabhṛdasīti kūrcaṃ dattvāpaḥ pādāviti pādau savyādi prakṣālayati sa dhautapādo virāja iti svahastena taddhastaṃ parimṛśya tenātmano hṛdayamabhimṛśati tato mayi teja ityarghyamācamanīyaṃ cādadītā mā ganyaśaseti madhuparkaṃ dadyāddevasya tveti pratigṛhya yanmadhuno madhavyamiti prāśnīyādyoge yoga ityācamyācamed amṛtāpidhānamasīti dhenuṃ baddhvā gaurdhenuriti tṛṇamuṣṭiṃ pradāya gaurasyapahateti saṃspṛśya tatsubhūtamiti visarjayati virāja iti pādyadānam ā mā ganyaśasety ācamanam amṛtopastaraṇam asīti madhuparkadānaṃ pṛthivīti tasyānnasaṃkalpanam amṛtāpidhānamasīti mukhavāsadānamiti viśeṣa ityeke ||
children.translated_text: Having seated him there, he gives the grass seat with “You are the bearer of sovereignty.” With “Waters are the feet,” he washes his feet, beginning with the left. When his feet have been washed, he touches that guest’s hand with his own hand, saying “Sovereign splendor,” and then touches his own heart with that hand. Then he should give the arghya and water for sipping with “May brilliance be in me.” He should give the madhuparka with “Do not go away from fame.” Receiving it with “Of the god,” he should eat it with “That sweetness which belongs to honey.” Having sipped with “In each joining,” he should sip again. With “You are the covering of immortality,” he ties up a cow; saying “A cow, a milch cow,” he gives a handful of grass; with “You are a cow; drive away,” he touches her, and with “May that be well-being,” he releases her. Some say that the special forms are these: giving water for the feet with “Sovereign splendor,” sipping with “Do not go away from fame,” giving the madhuparka with “You are the spread of immortality,” setting out his food with “Earth,” and giving mouth-fragrance with “You are the covering of immortality.”

children.text: dyaustvā dadātviti brāhmaṇānbhojayitvā indrāgnī me varca ityeṣāṃ praṇāmaṃ kuryātpuṇyāhaṃ vācayitvājyena vyāhṛtīrhutvā bāndhavaiḥ saha dhāma bhuñjīta madhudhāmnoścodanāyāṃ toyapiṣṭau pratinidhī gṛhṇīyādyasmādāpo vai sarvā devatāḥ sarvārthasādhakā iti vedyarthaṃ saṃbhārārthaṃ pṛthivī vanaspatayaḥ paśvarthamoṣadhaya iti vedānuśāsanaṃ bhavati ||
children.translated_text: After feeding the Brahmins with “May heaven give you,” he should bow to them with “<s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s> are my sacred brilliance.” Having had the auspicious day proclaimed and having offered the <s>vyāhṛtis</s> with clarified butter, he should eat the food together with his kinsmen. When honey and food are prescribed, he should take water and flour as substitutes, because the waters are indeed all the deities and accomplish every purpose. Thus the teaching of the Veda is that earth and forest-trees serve for the altar and materials, and herbs for cattle.

children.text: atha prāṇāgnihotravidhānaṃ svayaṃjyotirātmā yajamāno buddhiḥ patnī hṛdayapuṇḍarīkaṃ vedī romāṇi darbhāḥ prāṇo gārhapatyo 'pāna āhavanīyo vyāno 'nvāhārya udānaḥ sabhyaḥ samāna āvasathya iti pañcāgnayo bhavanti jihvādīndriyāṇi yajñapātrāṇi rasādayo viṣayā havīṃṣyasya phalam omarthāvāptis tadevam ekādhvaryurātmayajñaṃ saṃkalpyāmṛtopastaraṇam asītyannaṃ prokṣyānnasūktenābhimṛśyorjaskaram ityādhāvaṃ pītvāṅguṣṭhānāmikāmadhyamair ādāyānnaṃ prāṇāya svāhāpānāya svāhā vyānāya svāhodānāya svāhā samānāya svāheti pañcāhutīḥ pātraṃ spṛśanneva hutvorjaskaramiti punaścādhāvaṃ pītvāśnīyādācamyāpo gṛhītvādityābhimukhamoṃ prāṇānāpyāyasvetyudaram abhimṛśed dakṣiṇena karāṅguṣṭhāgreṇāṇor aṇīyāniti dakṣiṇapādāṅguṣṭhe saṃsrāvayedevaṃ sāyaṃprātaḥ prāṇāgnihotraṃ yajetātmayājinām idam ijyam agnihotraṃ yāvajjīvakamiti brahmavādino vadanti tadevaṃ bhuktvā gacchantamanṛṇo brahmapadamabhyetīti sāmapūrvaṃ mātā pitā gururvā paitṛkādikamṛṇatrayaṃ jāyamānasya brāhmaṇasya sahajātamityuktvā vārayediti vijñāyate ||
children.translated_text: Now the rule for the prāṇāgnihotra. The self, self-luminous, is the sacrificer; intellect is the wife; the lotus of the heart is the altar; the hairs are the sacrificial grasses; prāṇa is the gārhapatya fire, apāna the āhavanīya, vyāna the anvāhārya, udāna the sabhya, and samāna the āvasathya: these are the five fires. The sense organs beginning with the tongue are the sacrificial vessels; the objects beginning with tastes are the oblations; its fruit is the attainment of the meaning of oṃ. Thus, acting as the single adhvaryu, he resolves upon the self-sacrifice. Saying “You are the spread of immortality,” he sprinkles the food, touches it with the food hymn, drinks the rinsing water with “Strength-making,” takes food with the thumb, ring finger, and middle finger, and, while touching the vessel, offers five oblations: “To prāṇa, svāhā; to apāna, svāhā; to vyāna, svāhā; to udāna, svāhā; to samāna, svāhā.” Having drunk the rinsing water again with “Strength-making,” he should eat. After sipping water, taking water, facing <s>Āditya</s>, and saying “Oṃ, may you refresh the breaths,” he touches his belly. With the tip of the thumb of his right hand, saying “Smaller than the small,” he lets it flow onto the big toe of his right foot. In this way, evening and morning, he should perform the prāṇāgnihotra. The expounders of sacred knowledge say: this is the lifelong agnihotra to be sacrificed by those who sacrifice in the self. Having eaten in this way, one who goes forth, free from debt, reaches the state of <s>Brahman</s>. Reciting a <s>Sāman</s> first, the mother, father, or teacher should restrain him, saying that the three debts beginning with the paternal one arise together with a Brahmin at birth: so it is understood.

children.text: Chapter 3

athātaḥ pāṇigrahaṇamaṣṭau vivāhā bhavanti brāhmo daivaḥ prājāpatya ārṣa āsuro gāndharvo rākṣasaḥ paiśāca iti yadabhirūpaṃ vṛttavayaḥsampannam āhūyārhayitvā kanyālaṃkṛtā dāsyate sa brāhma iti gīyate yadṛtvijo yajñasyātmano 'laṃkṛtya kanyāṃ pratipādayati sa daivo yugapaddharmānuvartinau syātāmiti vācānumānyāgnikāryaṃ svayaṃ kṛtvā yatkanyāmarhayitvā dadyātsa prājāpatyo bhavati yadgomithunenaikena dvābhyāṃ vā kanyāṃ dadāti tamārṣamācakṣate yatkanyāmābharaṇamāropya śaktyā bandhubhyo dhanaṃ dattvāharate tamāsuramāmananti kāmayogo yadubhayoḥ sa gāndharvaḥ prasahya yatkanyāharaṇaṃ sa rākṣasaḥ suptāṃ pramattāṃ vā rahasi yadgacchati sa paiśāco bhavatītyeteṣāṃ prathame catvārastoyapradānapūrvakāḥ śastā brāhmaṇasya netare jaghanyā yasmāttrīnpūrvāṃstrīnaparān ārṣījātaḥ ṣaṭ pūrvānṣaḍaparānprājāpatyenoḍhāyā jātaḥ sapta pūrvānsaptāparāndaivīsuto daśa pūrvāndaśāparānātmānaṃ caikaviṃśatikaṃ brāhmīputraḥ pāvayediti ||
children.translated_text: Now, then, the taking of the hand. There are eight marriages: the <s>Brāhma</s>, <s>Daiva</s>, <s>Prājāpatya</s>, <s>Ārṣa</s>, <s>Āsura</s>, <s>Gāndharva</s>, <s>Rākṣasa</s>, and <s>Paiśāca</s>. When a maiden, adorned, is given after summoning and honoring a suitable man endowed with conduct and age, that is sung of as the <s>Brāhma</s>. When one presents an adorned maiden to the officiating priest of one's own sacrifice, that is the <s>Daiva</s>. When, after approving by the words, 'May the two of you together follow dharma,' and after oneself performing the fire rite, one honors and gives the maiden, that is the <s>Prājāpatya</s>. When one gives the maiden for one or two pairs of cows, they call that the <s>Ārṣa</s>. When one takes the maiden after placing ornaments on her and giving wealth, according to one's ability, to her kinsmen, they regard that as the <s>Āsura</s>. The union of desire on both sides is the <s>Gāndharva</s>. The forcible carrying off of a maiden is the <s>Rākṣasa</s>. When one approaches a sleeping or intoxicated woman in secret, that is the <s>Paiśāca</s>. Of these, the first four, preceded by the gift of water, are praised for a Brāhmaṇa, not the others, which are inferior. For a son born from an <s>Ārṣa</s> wife purifies three ancestors before and three after; a son born from a woman married by the <s>Prājāpatya</s> rite purifies six before and six after; a son of a <s>Daiva</s> wife purifies seven before and seven after; and the son of a <s>Brāhma</s> wife purifies ten before, ten after, and himself as the twenty-first.

children.text: māturasapiṇḍāṃ pitur asamānaṛṣigotrajātāṃ lakṣaṇasampannāṃ nagnikāṃ kanyāṃ varayitvā pañcāheṣu kulasya pariśuddhyai sapiṇḍaiḥ śrotriyaiḥ saha bhūtaṃ bhuñjīta yasmātsa pūto bhavatīti vijñāyate kanikradādinā kanyāgṛhaṃ gatvā pra su gmanteti tām īkṣitvābhrātṛghnīm iti tayekṣyamāṇo guruṇāgnimukhe kṛte kanyāprado varagotranāma śarmāntaṃ tathaitāmasya sahadharmacāriṇī bhavatīti brāhme vivāhe dharmaprajāsampattyarthaṃ yajñāpattyarthaṃ brahmadevarṣipitṛtṛptyarthaṃ prajāsahatvakarmabhyo dadāmītyudakena tāṃ dadyāt tāṃ prajāpatiḥ striyāmityudakena harate vastragandhābharaṇādīni saṃbhṛtya kanikradādinā kanyāgṛhaṃ saha bāndhavairgatvā teja āyuḥ śriyamiti vastrādinālaṃkṛtya prajāpatiḥ somamiti tathābharaṇamāropyādadītetyeke ||
children.translated_text: Having chosen a maiden who is not a <s>sapiṇḍa</s> of his mother, not born in the same seer-lineage and <s>gotra</s> as his father, endowed with auspicious marks, not previously connected with fire, he should, during five days, eat a pure meal with <s>sapiṇḍas</s> and learned <s>śrotriyas</s> for the purification of the family; for it is known that by this he becomes purified. Having gone to the maiden's house with the verse beginning <s>kanikradat</s>, and having looked at her with <s>pra su gmantā</s>, while she looks at him with <s>abhrātṛghnī</s>, and when the teacher has made the fire face them, the giver of the maiden, naming the groom's <s>gotra</s> and name ending in <s>śarman</s>, should say, 'This woman is to be his companion in dharma.' In a <s>Brāhma</s> marriage he should give her with water, saying, 'For the sake of dharma, offspring, and prosperity; for the sake of sacrificial continuity; for the satisfaction of <s>Brahman</s>, the gods, the seers, and the ancestors; for the rites connected with offspring, I give her.' He takes her with water with the formula <s>prajāpatiḥ striyām</s>. Having prepared garments, perfumes, ornaments, and the like, he goes with his kinsmen to the maiden's house with the verse beginning <s>kanikradat</s>, adorns her with garments and the rest with <s>teja āyuḥ śriyam</s>, places the ornament on her with <s>prajāpatiḥ somam</s>, and should take her. So some teach.

children.text: tataḥ saha snātāyā vadhvā navavastrālaṃkārāyāḥ puṇyāhānte pāṇiṃ gṛhītvā sumaṅgalīr iyaṃ vadhūrityagniśālāmāgatya prāṅmukhamāsayitvā tasyai śuddhāmbaraveṣaḥ kūrcaṃ dadāti tataḥ paristīryāgniraitvimāmagnistrāyatāṃ mā te gṛhe dyauste pṛṣṭham aprajastāṃ devakṛtamiti pañcavāruṇāntaṃ pradhānāñjuhuyādagneraparasyāmāstīrṇeṣu darbheṣvaśmānamātiṣṭheti vadhvāḥ pādāṅguṣṭhena dakṣiṇena sparśayati pratyaṅmukha iti pāṇigrahaṇaṃ sarasvatīti visargamaghoracakṣurityāsanaṃ ca kṛtvemāṃllājānityabhighāryeyaṃ nārīti tasyā lājāñjalinā juhoty udāyuṣety uttiṣṭhati pratyaṅmukha iti vadhūmukhekṣaṇaṃ sarasvatīti pāṇigrahaṇamaghoracakṣuriti visargamimāṃllājāniti lājapūraṇamiyaṃ nārīti homam udāyuṣety agnipraṇāmaṃ kuryādityeke ||
children.translated_text: Then, after the bride has bathed, is dressed in new garments and ornaments, and the auspicious-day rite has ended, he takes her hand and, with <s>sumaṅgalīr iyaṃ vadhūḥ</s>, comes to the fire hall. Having seated her facing east, he, dressed in clean white garments, gives her a brush of grass. Then, after spreading the grass around the fire, he should offer the principal oblations with <s>agnir aitv imām</s>, <s>agnis trāyatām</s>, <s>mā te gṛhe</s>, <s>dyauḥ te pṛṣṭham</s>, and <s>aprajastām devakṛtam</s>, ending with the five <s>Vāruṇa</s> formulas. On darbha grass spread west of the fire, with <s>aśmānam ātiṣṭha</s>, he makes the bride touch a stone with the big toe of her right foot. With <s>pratyaṅmukhaḥ</s> he performs the taking of the hand; with <s>sarasvatī</s>, the release; with <s>aghoracakṣuḥ</s>, the seating. Having anointed the parched grain with <s>imān lājān</s>, he offers her parched grain with her joined handfuls with <s>iyaṃ nārī</s>. With <s>ud āyuṣā</s> he rises. Or, according to some, with <s>pratyaṅmukhaḥ</s> he looks at the bride's face; with <s>sarasvatī</s> he takes the hand; with <s>aghoracakṣuḥ</s> he releases; with <s>imān lājān</s> he fills the parched grain; with <s>iyaṃ nārī</s> he makes the oblation; and with <s>ud āyuṣā</s> he bows to the fire.

children.text: viśvā uta tvayetyagniṃ pradakṣiṇaṃ kṛtvātigāhemahi dviṣa ityāsitvā tridhaivaṃ lājahomaṃ juhuyāttato mūlahomānte 'gniṃ patighnyantaṃ vāyuḥ ninditāntamādityaṃ ghorāntaṃ gandharvaṃ yaśoghnyantaṃ candraṃ putraghnyantaṃ hutvā vyāhṛtiḥ prāsāvīr ityantaiś caturbhiḥ pravāhaṇaṃ kṛtvā punaḥ paristīrya sviṣṭakṛnmindāhutī vicchinnamṛddhisaptasamidvyāhṛtīśca juhuyādagneraparasyāmāstīryodagagrānsapta barhiṣo vadhvā saha dakṣiṇena pādenaikam iṣe viṣṇuriti dve ūrja iti trīṇi vratāyeti catvārīti pañca paśubhya iti ṣaḍ rāyaspoṣāyeti sapta saptabhya iti tānparyāyeṇākramya gatvā sakheti nivarteta mama hṛdaya iti tasyā hṛdayamabhimṛśati prokṣaṇaiḥ prokṣya puṇyāhaṃ svastighoṣeṇārundhatīndrāṇyaditiḥ śrīriveti vadhvā manuḥ prajāpatiḥ puruṣottamo mahendra iveti varasya ca catvāri stomāny āropayeyur iti pāṇigrahaṇaṃ dhruvadarśanāntamityeke tataḥ prabhṛti gārhasthyaṃ dharmamanutiṣṭhatīti vijñāyate ||
children.translated_text: Having gone clockwise around the fire with <s>viśvā uta tvayā</s>, he sits with <s>atigāhemahi dviṣaḥ</s> and should offer the parched-grain oblation three times in this way. Then, at the end of the basic oblation, he offers to <s>Agni</s> with the formula ending in <s>patighnī</s>, to <s>Vāyu</s> with that ending in <s>ninditā</s>, to <s>Āditya</s> with that ending in <s>ghorā</s>, to <s>Gandharva</s> with that ending in <s>yaśoghnī</s>, and to <s>Candra</s> with that ending in <s>putraghnī</s>. Having performed the carrying forward with the four formulas ending in <s>vyāhṛtiḥ prāsāvīḥ</s>, he again spreads the grass around the fire and offers the <s>sviṣṭakṛt</s>, the <s>mindāhutis</s>, the oblation for what is broken, the prosperity oblation, seven fuel sticks, and the <s>vyāhṛtis</s>. Having spread, west of the fire, seven blades of sacrificial grass with their tips northward, he goes with the bride, stepping on them in turn with the right foot: one step with <s>iṣe viṣṇuḥ</s>, two with <s>ūrje</s>, three with <s>vratāya</s>, four with <s>paśubhyaḥ</s>, five with <s>rāyaspoṣāya</s>, six with <s>saptabhyaḥ</s>, and seven; then with <s>sakhe</s> he turns back. With <s>mama hṛdaye</s> he touches her heart. Having sprinkled her with sprinkling water, accompanied by the proclamation of an auspicious day and welfare, they should place upon the bride the four praises, 'like <s>Arundhatī</s>, <s>Indrāṇī</s>, <s>Aditi</s>, and <s>Śrī</s>,' and upon the groom, 'like <s>Manu</s>, <s>Prajāpati</s>, <s>Puruṣottama</s>, and great <s>Indra</s>.' Some say that the taking of the hand extends as far as showing the pole star. From that time onward he performs the dharma of a householder; so it is understood.

children.text: atha caturthīvāso vaivāhikamagniṃ vadhvā sahādāya sampravāhārayanviti vadhūṃ samaṃ vadhvetyagniṃ saṃśāsti dakṣiṇaṃ pādamagre 'tihara dehaliṃ mādhiṣṭhā ityāvasathe praviśya prācyāmardhe samādadhītāgneraparasyāmānaḍuhaṃ carma lohitaṃ kṛṣṇājinaṃ vā prācīnagrīvamuttaralomāstṛṇāti tatra prāṅmukham udaṅmukhaṃ vā vadhūmupaveśya patiriha gāvaḥ prajāyadhvamiti paścān niṣīdetā jyotiṣāṃ darśanād vācaṃyamāvanyatarānupetāvāsātām udite nakṣatre prācīmudīcīṃ vā devīḥ ṣaḍ urvīr iti diśamupasthāya mā hāsmahi prajayeti candraṃ saptarṣaya iti saptarṣīnkṛttikā nakṣatrāṇyarundhatīṃ ca dhruvakṣitiriti dhruvaṃ ca dṛṣṭvopatiṣṭheyātāṃ manojñaṃ tayā saha sambhāṣyāthāgneyaḥ sthālīpākaḥ prajā sthālīmiti sthālīmabhimṛśyāgnaye juṣṭaṃ nirvapāmīti sthālyāṃ taṇḍulānnirvāpya vācaspataye pavasveti vadhvā caruṃ śrapayatyabhighāryodagudvāsya paristīryāgnimupasamādhāya havyavāhamiti sviṣṭakṛtā yajeta hutaśeṣeṇa śrotriyaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ tarpayitvā tasmā ṛṣabhaṃ dattvānṛṇo bhavatīti vijñāyate ||
children.translated_text: Then, on the fourth night, taking the marriage fire together with the bride, and while they make it flow onward, as it were, he instructs the bride with, 'Together with the bride,' and the fire with, 'Together with the bride.' Saying, 'Put the right foot forward; do not step on the threshold,' he enters the dwelling. In the eastern half he should establish the fire. West of the fire he spreads a red bull's hide, or a black antelope skin, with its neck toward the east and the hair upward. Having seated the bride there facing east or north, the husband should sit behind her with, 'Here may cows be born.' Until the stars are seen they should remain silent and sit, not approaching one another for intercourse. When the lunar mansion has risen, facing east or north, they should attend upon the direction with, 'O goddesses, six broad ones'; upon the moon with, 'May we not be deprived of offspring'; upon the Seven Seers with, 'The Seven Seers'; upon the <s>Kṛttikās</s>, the lunar mansions, and <s>Arundhatī</s>; and upon <s>Dhruva</s> with, 'Firm is the dwelling.' Having seen these, they should attend upon them. After conversing pleasantly with her, the <s>Āgneya</s> pot-offering follows. Touching the pot with, 'The pot is offspring,' and depositing rice-grains in the pot with, 'I deposit what is pleasing to <s>Agni</s>,' he has the bride cook the <s>caru</s> with, 'Purify yourself for <s>Vācaspati</s>.' Having sprinkled it with ghee, taken it off northward, spread the grass, and set the fire in order, he should sacrifice with the <s>sviṣṭakṛt</s> using, 'Carrier of oblations.' With the remnant of the offering he satisfies a learned <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, gives him a bull, and thereby, it is understood, becomes free of debt.

children.text: ata ūrdhvaṃ parvaṇi sthālīpākena yajeta nityaṃ yavairvrīhibhirvā hastena sūryāya svāhā prajāpataye svāheti prātarāhutī agnaye svāhā prajāpataye svāheti sāyamāhutī juhuyādagnyantarasaṃsarge 'nugate vā patnī kṛcchraṃ carati śrotriyāgārānmathitvā vāgnimādāya punar aupāsanam ādadhītodakyāśucyādisaṃsarge ca vidhānaṃ yajñaprāyaścitte vakṣyāmo viyoge pakṣasyopāvaroheti samidhaṃ yāvatkṛṣṇaṃ tāvattaptvā samāropya gacchedaharahastāṃ prajvālya hutvā tathānyāṃ samidhaṃ nidadhāti ||
children.translated_text: After this, on each festival day, he should sacrifice with a pot-offering. Every day he should offer morning oblations by hand with barley or rice, saying, 'To <s>Sūrya</s>, svāhā; to <s>Prajāpati</s>, svāhā,' and evening oblations with, 'To <s>Agni</s>, svāhā; to <s>Prajāpati</s>, svāhā.' If another fire comes into contact with it, or if it goes out, the wife performs a <s>kṛcchra</s> penance; or, after churning fire from the house of a learned <s>śrotriya</s>, he should take the fire and again establish the <s>aupāsana</s> fire. The rule for contact with a menstruating woman, impurity, and the like we shall state under sacrificial expiation. In separation, with, 'At the descent of the fortnight,' he should heat a fuel-stick as far as it is blackened, place the fire upon it, and depart; day by day he kindles that same fuel-stick, offers, and likewise lays down another fuel-stick.

children.text: pacane vāvasathye carumabhighārya vaiśvadevaṃ yathā heti maṇḍalaṃ pradakṣiṇamupalipya parimṛjyāgnaye svāhā somāya svāhetyuttaradakṣiṇayormadhye vyāhṛtīrviśvebhyo devebhyaḥ svāhā dhanvantaraye svāhā kuhvai svāhānumatyai svāhā prajāpataye svāhā dyāvāpṛthivībhyām svāhā vyāhṛtīrimā me agna iti caruṃ sedhmaṃ juhuyādagnihotrāya svāhā vaiśvadevayajñāya svāhā brahmayajñāya svāhā devayajñāya svāhā bhūtayajñāya svāhā manuṣyayajñāya svāhā pitṛyajñāya svadhā namaḥ svāhā pañcamahāyajñāya svāhā vyāhṛtīḥ sviṣṭakṛdvyāhṛtīratha gṛhadevatābhyo yathādiśaṃ baliharaṇaṃ brahmaṇe namo brahmapuruṣebhyo namo vāstoṣpataye nama iti gṛhamadhye indrāya nama indrapuruṣebhyo namo yamāya namo yamapuruṣebhyo namo varuṇāya namo varuṇapuruṣebhyo namaḥ somāya namaḥ somapuruṣebhyo namo 'gnaye namo nirṛtaye namo vāyave nama īśānāya nama iti sarvaṃ dakṣiṇe pitṛbhyo jñātivargapatnyantebhyaḥ kṛtopavītī yāvanto 'nnārthinastāvadbhyo nirvapāmīti nirūpyākāśe viśvebhyo devebhyo namo divācarebhyo namo bhūtebhyo namo naktaṃcarebhyo nama ityucchīrṣake śriyā iti pādato bhadrakālyā iti pratidvāraṃ pūrvāntam uttarāntaṃ vā bhuvaṃgayor marudbhya iti culyāḥ pakṣayoragnaya ityudadhānyām adbhya iti peṣaṇyorubhayordṛṣada ityulūkhalamusalayorvanaspatibhya iti śūrpa oṣadhībhya iti vāstupṛṣṭhe śunāṃ ca patitānāṃ ca śvapacāṃ pāparogiṇām vayasāṃ ca krimīṇāṃ ca bhūmāvannaṃ vapāmyahamiti baliśeṣaṃ nirvapati pūrvavat pravāhaṇaṃ kṛtvā bhūtiḥ smeti bhasmālipyāpo hi ṣṭheti prokṣya yatte agne tejastenetyagnim ud vayamityādityaṃ copatiṣṭheta nityaṃ sāyaṃprātaḥ patnī vā puṣṭikāmā baliṃ haredvaiśvadevakāle prāptamatithiṃ śaktyā tarpayedvaiśvānaro hyeṣa bhavati ||
children.translated_text: Or, in the cooking fire or household fire, having sprinkled the <s>caru</s> with ghee, he performs the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s>. Wiping a circular space clockwise as before, he should offer in the middle between north and south, 'To <s>Agni</s>, svāhā; to <s>Soma</s>, svāhā,' then the <s>vyāhṛtis</s>, 'To all the gods, svāhā; to <s>Dhanvantari</s>, svāhā; to <s>Kuhū</s>, svāhā; to <s>Anumatī</s>, svāhā; to <s>Prajāpati</s>, svāhā; to Heaven and Earth, svāhā,' the <s>vyāhṛtis</s>, and, with 'These of mine, O <s>Agni</s>,' the <s>caru</s> together with fuel. He should offer, 'To the <s>Agnihotra</s>, svāhā; to the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> sacrifice, svāhā; to the <s>Brahmayajña</s>, svāhā; to the god-sacrifice, svāhā; to the being-sacrifice, svāhā; to the human-sacrifice, svāhā; to the ancestor-sacrifice, svadhā, homage, svāhā; to the five great sacrifices, svāhā,' then the <s>vyāhṛtis</s>, the <s>sviṣṭakṛt</s>, and the <s>vyāhṛtis</s>. Then he makes bali offerings to the household deities according to direction: in the middle of the house, 'Homage to <s>Brahman</s>; homage to the men of <s>Brahman</s>; homage to <s>Vāstoṣpati</s>'; then, 'Homage to <s>Indra</s>; homage to the men of <s>Indra</s>; homage to <s>Yama</s>; homage to the men of <s>Yama</s>; homage to <s>Varuṇa</s>; homage to the men of <s>Varuṇa</s>; homage to <s>Soma</s>; homage to the men of <s>Soma</s>; homage to <s>Agni</s>; homage to <s>Nirṛti</s>; homage to <s>Vāyu</s>; homage to <s>Īśāna</s>.' All of this is on the southern side. Wearing the sacred thread over the right shoulder, he deposits food for the ancestors, the groups of kinsmen, and the wives belonging to them, saying, 'For as many as desire food, for that many I deposit.' In the open air he says, 'Homage to all the gods; homage to those who move by day; homage to beings; homage to those who move by night.' At the head of the bed he offers with, 'To <s>Śrī</s>'; at the foot with, 'To <s>Bhadrakālī</s>'; at each doorway, beginning either from the east or from the north; to the serpents with, 'To the serpents'; on the two sides of the hearth with, 'To the <s>Maruts</s>'; at the water-pot with, 'To the fires'; at the grinding stones with, 'To the waters'; at both mortar and pestle with, 'To the stones'; at the winnowing basket with, 'To the forest-lords'; and at the back of the house with, 'To the herbs.' Saying, 'For dogs, for the fallen, for dog-cookers, for the sinfully diseased, for birds, and for worms, I scatter food on the ground,' he deposits the remainder of the bali. Having performed the carrying-forward as before, he smears himself with ash with, 'Prosperity are we,' sprinkles with <s>āpo hi ṣṭhā</s>, and attends upon the fire with, 'With that splendor of yours, O <s>Agni</s>,' and upon <s>Āditya</s> with, 'Upward we.' Daily, evening and morning, or the wife if she desires prosperity, should make the bali offering. At the time of the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s>, he should satisfy, according to his ability, a guest who has arrived, for such a guest is indeed <s>Vaiśvānara</s>.

children.text: tadevaṃ trirātram haviṣyāśinau brahmacāriṇau dhautavastravratacāriṇau syātāṃ tato 'parasyāṃ rātrau caturthyām alaṃkṛtyāgnim upasamādhāya nava prāyaścittāni juhuyādagne vāyavādityāditya vāyavagne 'gne vāyavāditya vyāhṛtir bhūrbhanam iti caturbhirvadhūmūrdhnyājyena juhuyādagniṃ pradakṣiṇaṃ kṛtvā prācyāmudīcyāṃ vā tām upaveśyābhiṣṭvā pañcaśākheneti yonimabhimṛśya saṃ nā mana ityupagacchedimām anuvratetyāliṅganaṃ madhu he madhvidamiti maithunaṃ kurvīta suprajāstvāyetyupagamanaṃ saṃ nā mana ityāliṅganam imāmanuvrateti vadhūmukhekṣaṇamityeke ||
children.translated_text: In this way, for three nights the two should eat sacrificial food, remain continent, wear washed garments, and observe the vow. Then on the next night, the fourth, having adorned himself, having placed the fire near, he should offer nine expiatory oblations: to <s>Agni</s>, to <s>Vāyu</s>, to <s>Āditya</s>; to <s>Āditya</s>, to <s>Vāyu</s>, to <s>Agni</s>; to <s>Agni</s>, <s>Vāyu</s>, and <s>Āditya</s>; and the <s>vyāhṛti</s>, '<s>bhūḥ</s>, <s>bhuvaḥ</s>.' With four formulas he should offer clarified butter on the bride's head. Having circumambulated the fire clockwise, he seats her to the east or north. After sprinkling her with '<s>abhiṣ ṭvā</s>,' he touches the womb with '<s>pañcaśākhena</s>.' With '<s>saṃ nā manaḥ</s>' he approaches her; with '<s>imām anuvratā</s>' he embraces her; with '<s>madhu he madhvidam</s>' he performs intercourse; with '<s>suprajās tvā</s>' he approaches her. Some say that '<s>saṃ nā manaḥ</s>' is for the embrace, and '<s>imām anuvratā</s>' for looking at the bride's face.

children.text: atha trirātramṛtau malavadvāsāḥ snānāñjanādīni varjayed ekabhaktā syād akharveṇāñjalināyasena vā pibenna śulbenāśnāti na grahānīkṣeta na divā svaped yathoktaṃ vrataṃ kuryāc caturthyāṃ dantadhāvanaṃ gandhāmalakādibhiḥ snātvā śvetavastrānulepanā strīśūdrābhyām anabhibhāṣyāparam adṛṣṭvā bhartāraṃ paśyed yasmādṛtusnātā yādṛśaṃ puruṣaṃ paśyettādṛśī prajā bhavati ṛturātrayo dvādaśa bhavanti ṣoḍaśeti cācakṣate prathamās tisro na gamyāḥ pumān samāsu viṣamāsu strī jāyate śālivrīhiyavānāmannaṃ payasā prāśnīyād yasmādāhāramūlā dhātavo bhavanti lakṣmīvaṭaśuṅgasahadevīnām anyatamam abhiṣūya prakṣipeddakṣiṇe nāsāpuṭe putrakāmāyā vāme strīkāmāyā na niṣṭhīvanaṃ kuryācchokaroṣau varjayati tata enāṃ yanme garbhādibhiḥ prokṣaṇaiḥ prokṣya viṣṇuryoniṃ kalpayatviti tāmupagacchet pariṣicya vaiśvadevaṃ vaiṣṇavaṃ mūlahomāṅgahomau hutvā viṣṇuryoniṃ kalpayatvityupagamanamityeke ||
children.translated_text: Now, for three nights during her menstrual period she should wear a soiled garment, avoid bathing, collyrium, and the like, eat only one meal, and drink from a non-dwarfish handful or from an iron vessel; she does not eat from copper, does not look at the planets, and does not sleep by day. She should observe the vow as stated. On the fourth day, after cleaning her teeth and bathing with fragrant substances, āmalaka, and the like, wearing white garments and unguents, not spoken to by women or <s>Śūdras</s>, and not seeing anyone else, she should look at her husband; for, when a woman has bathed after menstruation, the kind of man she sees is the kind of offspring she has. The nights of the season are twelve; some say sixteen. The first three are not to be approached. A male is born on even nights, a female on odd nights. She should eat food of śāli rice, vrīhi rice, and barley with milk, because the bodily constituents are rooted in food. If she desires a son, one should press any one of <s>lakṣmī</s>, a shoot of the banyan, or <s>sahadevī</s>, and put it into the right nostril; if she desires a daughter, into the left. She should not spit; she avoids grief and anger. Then, sprinkling her with the sprinklings beginning '<s>yan me garbha</s>,' he should approach her with '<s>Viṣṇu</s> shall prepare the womb.' Having sprinkled around, having offered the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s>, the Vaiṣṇava oblation, the principal oblation, and the ancillary oblations, some say that the approach is with '<s>Viṣṇu</s> shall prepare the womb.'

children.text: atha gṛhītagarbhāliṅgāni śarīrāṭopaḥ sakthisīdanaṃ dveṣo bharturarucirāhāro lālāprakopaḥ kharatā vācaḥ sphuraṇaṃ yoneriti garbhasya daivānubandhaṃ jñātvāpūryamāṇapakṣe puṇye puṃnāmni śubhe nakṣatra ājyenāghāraṃ hutvā tāṃ maṅgalayuktām upaveśya pariṣicya dhātādi pañca vāruṇaṃ mūlahomaṃ sviṣṭākāraṃ ca hutvā vṛṣo 'sīti yavāndadāti payo dadhi ghṛtaṃ samaṃ gṛhītaṃ trivṛdityāmananti bhūstvayi dadāmītyenāṃ trivṛtprāśayedācāntāyā nābherūrdhvam ābhiṣṭvāhaṃ parāñceti darbheṇa trir unmārjya puṇyāhaṃ kuryādbrāhmaṇānannena tarpayati ||
children.translated_text: Now the signs that pregnancy has been conceived are swelling of the body, weakness of the thighs, aversion toward the husband, distaste for food, excessive salivation, roughness of speech, and throbbing of the womb. Having recognized the divine connection of the embryo, in the waxing fortnight, under an auspicious lunar mansion with a male name, after offering the <s>āghāra</s> with clarified butter, he seats her adorned with auspicious things, sprinkles around, and offers the five oblations beginning with <s>Dhātṛ</s>, the Vāruṇa oblation, the principal oblation, and the <s>sviṣṭākāra</s>. Saying '<s>vṛṣo 'si</s>,' he gives her barley grains. Milk, curd, and ghee are taken in equal measure; they call this <s>trivṛt</s>. With '<s>bhūs tvayi dadāmi</s>' he should make her eat the <s>trivṛt</s>. When she has sipped water, he sprinkles her above the navel, wipes upward three times with a blade of <s>darbha</s> while saying '<s>ahaṃ parāñci</s>,' performs the auspicious-day rite, and satisfies Brahmins with food.

children.text: atha garbhādhānādicaturthe māsi puṃsavanaṃ bhavati śuklapakṣe śuddhe 'hani pūrvāhṇe 'gnimupasamādhāya pūrvavat sviṣṭakārāntaṃ hutvā dakṣiṇato 'gneraparasyāmāsīnāyā vṛṣo 'sīti sarṣapamiśritānyavānāṇḍau stha iti dadyād alābhe māṣadhānyau pratinidhī syātām oṃ bhūrbhuvaḥ suvo rākāmahaṃ yāste rāke soma eva viśvā uta tvayetyudaramabhimṛśet pūrvavat trivṛt prāśanādīnīti vijñāyate ||
children.translated_text: Now, in the fourth month from conception and the other preceding rites, the <s>puṃsavana</s> takes place. In the bright fortnight, on a pure day, in the forenoon, having placed the fire near and having offered as before up to the <s>sviṣṭakṛt</s>, he gives, to the woman seated west of the fire on its southern side, grains of barley mixed with mustard, saying '<s>vṛṣo 'si</s>' and '<s>aṇḍau stha</s>.' If these are unavailable, two grains of black gram or other grain may be substitutes. With 'Oṃ, <s>bhūr bhuvaḥ suvaḥ</s>; O <s>Rākā</s>, I ...; those of yours, O <s>Rākā</s>; <s>Soma</s> indeed; all, and you,' he should touch her belly. The <s>trivṛt</s> eating and the rest are to be understood as before.

children.text: atha garbhādhānādyaṣṭame māsi sīmantonnayanaṃ kuryātpakṣo dinaṃ ca vyākhyātaṃ pūrvavad dhātādi hutvā treṇyā śalalyā saha śalāṭuglapsaṃ sāgrapattraṃ kuśāṅkuraṃ ca darbheṇa trirābadhyoṃ bhūrbhuvaḥ suvar iti gṛhītvā tasyāstathāsīnāyāḥ sraggandhavatyāḥ sīmante rākāmahaṃ yāste rāka iti sthāpayitvonnayanaṃ kuryātsoma eveti purastādiva kuryātpūrvavattrivṛtprāśanaṃ puṇyāhāntamityeke ||
children.translated_text: Now, in the eighth month from conception and the other rites, he should perform the <s>sīmantonnayana</s>. The fortnight and day have been explained. Having offered, as before, the oblations beginning with <s>Dhātṛ</s>, he binds three times with <s>darbha</s> a three-pointed porcupine quill, together with an unripe fig, a leaf with its tip, and a shoot of <s>kuśa</s>; taking it with 'Oṃ, <s>bhūr bhuvaḥ suvaḥ</s>,' he places it on the hair-parting of her, seated as before, wearing garlands and scents, with '<s>rākām ahaṃ yās te rāke</s>,' and performs the parting upward. With '<s>soma eva</s>' he should perform it as before in front. Some say that the <s>trivṛt</s> eating and the rite up to the auspicious-day proclamation are as before.

children.text: atha viṣṇubalim uttarapraṇidhāvagnyādīndevānoṃ bhūḥ puruṣamoṃ bhuvaḥ puruṣom suvaḥ puruṣamoṃ bhūrbhuvaḥ suvaḥ puruṣaṃ cetyāvāhya tathaiva nirvāpādyāghāraṃ hutvāgneḥ pūrvasyāṃ darbhāsaneṣu keśavaṃ nārāyaṇaṃ mādhavaṃ govindaṃ viṣṇuṃ madhusūdanaṃ trivikramaṃ vāmanaṃ śrīdharaṃ hṛṣīkeśaṃ padmanābhaṃ dāmodaramiti nāmabhirdevaṃ viṣṇum āvāhyāpohiraṇyapavamānaiḥ snāpayitvā tattannāmnārcayatyato devādyairviṣṇornu kaṃ tadasya priyaṃ pra tadviṣṇuḥ paromātrayā vicakrame trirdeva iti dvādaśāhutīrājyena hutvā pāyasamājyasaṃyuktaṃ havirdevaṃ nivedya dvādaśanāmabhirato devādyair viṣṇor nukādyair ājyamiśraṃ pāyasaṃ juhuyād ṛgyajuḥsāmātharvabhir mantrair vaiṣṇavairdevaṃ saṃstūya namo 'ntairnāmabhiḥ praṇametpāyasaśeṣaṃ patnīṃ prāśayati ||
children.translated_text: Now, for the <s>Viṣṇu-bali</s>, at the northern praṇidhi he invokes the deities beginning with <s>Agni</s> and the Person with 'Oṃ <s>bhūḥ</s>, <s>Puruṣa</s>; Oṃ <s>bhuvaḥ</s>, <s>Puruṣa</s>; Oṃ <s>suvaḥ</s>, <s>Puruṣa</s>; Oṃ <s>bhūr bhuvaḥ suvaḥ</s>, <s>Puruṣa</s>.' Having in the same way performed the setting out and the other preliminaries and offered the <s>āghāra</s>, he invokes the god <s>Viṣṇu</s> on seats of <s>darbha</s> east of the fire by the names <s>Keśava</s>, <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, <s>Mādhava</s>, <s>Govinda</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Madhusūdana</s>, <s>Trivikrama</s>, <s>Vāmana</s>, <s>Śrīdhara</s>, <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s>, <s>Padmanābha</s>, and <s>Dāmodara</s>. He bathes him with the water, gold, and purifying verses, and worships him with each respective name. Then, with the verses beginning '<s>ato devāḥ</s>,' '<s>viṣṇor nu kam</s>,' '<s>tad asya priyam</s>,' '<s>pra tad viṣṇuḥ</s>,' '<s>paro mātrayā</s>,' '<s>vicakrame</s>,' and '<s>trir devaḥ</s>,' he offers twelve oblations of clarified butter. Having presented to the deity an oblation of milk-rice mixed with clarified butter, he should offer milk-rice mixed with clarified butter using the twelve names and the verses beginning '<s>ato devāḥ</s>' and '<s>viṣṇor nu kam</s>.' With Vaiṣṇava mantras from the <s>Ṛgveda</s>, <s>Yajurveda</s>, <s>Sāmaveda</s>, and <s>Atharvaveda</s>, he praises the deity; with names ending in 'homage' he bows down. He makes his wife eat the remainder of the milk-rice.

children.text: atha jātakarma vyākhyāsyāmo 'riṣṭāgāraṃ yathoktaṃ kṛtvā vṛṣabhoṣitaṃ tilasarṣapairdhūpayitvā tāṃ praveśayettajjñāḥ striyas tisraś catasro vā parigṛhyaināṃ saṃvāhayeyuḥ kukṣau śithile hṛdayabandhaṃ muktvā saśūle jaghane prajāyata ityavadhārayet garbhasaṅge viśalyāṃ suvarcalāṃ vā yonau niṣpīḍya nidadhyāddhūpayetpiṇḍītakenāhikṛttyā vā yoniṃ hiraṇyapuṣpyā mūlaṃ hastapādayorādadhāti yadā nāsāgraṃ dṛśyate tadāsya grahasthitiṃ jñātvā śubhāśubhaṃ parīkṣeta yasmāt tadguṇānvitaṃ vardhayejjāyamāne mātur udakumbhaṃ dakṣiṇataḥ śirobhāge sthāpayitvā tatastūryantīṃ pādato nidhāya yathaiva somaḥ pavata ityudaramabhimṛśetkumāre jāte dvāravāme 'śmani paraśuṃ tasminhiraṇyaṃ sthāpayitvāśmā bhavetyadharamuttaraṃ karoti tasyoparyaṅgādaṅgāditi kumāramekayā striyā dhārayettamadbhirabhyukṣya tilade 'vapadyasveti satilamakṣataṃ mūrdhnyādhāyaupāsanamaraṇyāṃ nirharati ||
children.translated_text: Now we shall explain the birth rite. Having prepared the lying-in chamber as prescribed, fumigated it with bull-dung smoke and sesame and mustard seeds, he should bring her in. Three or four women who know that rite should take charge of her and massage her. When the belly is slackened, and when the binding at the heart has loosened and there is pain in the lower body, he should ascertain, 'she is giving birth.' If the fetus is obstructed, he should squeeze and place in the vagina viśalyā or suvarcalā, and fumigate the womb with piṇḍītaka or ahikṛttyā. He places the root of hiraṇyapuṣpī on the hands and feet. When the tip of the nose is seen, then, knowing the position of the planets, he should examine the auspicious and inauspicious result, since one should raise the newborn in accordance with those qualities. When the child is being born, he should set a water jar to the mother's right, near the head. Then, laying the laboring woman down from the feet upward, he should stroke her belly with 'As <s>Soma</s> purifies himself.' When a boy has been born, he should place an axe on a stone at the left of the doorway, and gold on that; with 'Be a stone' he turns the lower jaw upward. Above him, with 'From limb to limb,' he should have one woman hold the boy. He sprinkles him with water, places sesame-mixed unbroken rice on his head with 'Fall upon the giver of sesame,' and takes the fire-drill for the domestic fire out from the fire-drill wood.

children.text: cullyāṃ kapālamāropya vṛṣabhaśakṛtpiṇḍair jātakāgniṃ sādhayettamenamuttapanīyamityudāharanti tenaiva dhūpaṃ dadyāddvārasya dakṣiṇato nidhāyāṅgāravarṇe paristīrya kaṇasarṣapairhastena śaṇḍe ratho 'yaḥ śaṇḍo marka ālikhanvilikhannaryamṇa āntrīmukhaḥ keśinīretān ghnataitān pūrva eṣāṃ miśravāsaso naktaṃcāriṇo niśīthacāriṇī tāsāṃ tvamayaṃ te yonirmama nāmeti vyāhṛtīśca hutvā prakṣālya pāṇimavanīmālabhya yatte susīma iti medhāyai ghṛtaṃ karoti vacā pathyā hiraṇyaṃ madhu sarpiriti medhājananāni bhavanti brāhmīghṛtaṃ payo vacādhikaṃ cāmananti suvarṇaṃ darbheṇa baddhvāntardhāya ghṛtaṃ bhūrṛca iti prāṅmukhaṃ prāśayati nityaṃ sāyaṃprātarevamaharaharhutvā medhāyai pāyayed uṣṇaśītābhir adbhirenaṃ snāpayitvā kṣetriyai tveti nītvā yā daivīriti māturaṅke sthāpayitvā tāsāṃ tveti stanau prakṣālyāyaṃ kumāra iti dakṣiṇādi pāyayedāpo haviṣṣviti nyastamudakumbhaṃ śodhayitvā nityaṃ sāyaṃprātar ādadhāti tathaiva ghṛtaprāśanāntaṃ karma kṛtvā snātvaupāsananirharaṇādi karotītyeke tṛtīye pañcame saptame navame cāhni śayanādikaṃ śodhayatīti ||
children.translated_text: Having set a potsherd on the hearth, he should prepare the birth fire with lumps of bull dung; they call this fire the uttapanīya. With that same fire he should give fumigation. Placing it south of the door, when it has the color of embers he should spread grass around it and, with grain and mustard seeds in his hand, offer with the formulas beginning, 'O eunuch, this chariot; O eunuch, O monkey,' 'Scratching and tearing,' 'O intestine-mouthed one of <s>Aryaman</s>,' 'O hairy one, slay these, slay these; before them are those of mixed garments, night-wanderers and midnight-wanderers; this is their womb; my name is yours,' and the <s>vyāhṛtis</s>. Having washed his hand and touched the ground, with 'What is yours, O well-bounded one,' he prepares clarified butter for intelligence. Vacā, pathyā, gold, honey, and ghee are substances that generate intelligence; they also teach clarified butter with brāhmī, milk, and more vacā. Binding gold with darbha grass and concealing it, he feeds the child ghee while facing east, with the <s>bhūr</s> verse. In this same way, after offering daily, evening and morning, he should feed him for intelligence. Having bathed him with warm and cool waters, with 'For the field-born affliction' he carries him away; with 'She who is divine' he places him in the mother's lap. Washing her breasts with 'Of these, you,' he should have him drink beginning with the right breast with 'This boy.' Having purified the water jar set down with 'The waters among the oblations,' he sets it in place regularly evening and morning. Some say that, in the same way, after performing the rite up to the feeding of ghee, he bathes and performs the acts beginning with taking out the domestic fire; and that on the third, fifth, seventh, and ninth day he purifies the bed and the other things.

children.text: atha vāstusavanaṃ vyākhyāsyāmo nave vāstunyuṣite 'pi sūtakapretakayorvāpayitvā mṛnmayāni bhāṇḍāni purāṇāni tyaktvā navāni parigṛhyānyānparicchadānyathoktaṃ śodhayitvā bhūmiyajñeneṣṭvā nivasedyasmādvāstusavanena śuddhivastūnām āghāro vāstusavanasya vāstoṣpate pratijānīhi vāstoṣpate śagmayeti dvābhyāṃ yajeta bhūmiyajñāya svāhā yajñadaivataṃ pra sodaryai svāheti dvau bhūmiyajñadaivatyau medinī devī devī hiraṇyagarbhiṇī samudravatī sāvitrī śṛṅge śṛṅge vāyuparī jalaśayanīti pañca bhūmidaivatyā vyāhṛtīrhutvā puṇyāhamahamagne agniṃ gṛhṇāmītyagniṣṭhād darbhapūlenāgniṃ gṛhītvā prathamādaindrādbhuvaṃgādārabhya vāstunaḥ kuḍyamūlādbahirantaśca vāmaṃ parītyā brahmasthānāt paryagniṃ kārayitvāparadvāreṇa visṛjettathaivāṇor aṇīyān iti pātreṇānvapaḥ srāvayitvā śiṣṭābhiḥ sarvatra prokṣayatyevaṃ vāruṇādbhuvaṃgādvā yāmyātsaumyādārabhya paryagnyādhāvasrutī syātām ||
children.translated_text: Now we shall explain the <s>vāstusavana</s> (dwelling-purification rite). When one has occupied a new dwelling, or after birth or death impurity, he should have the clay vessels washed, discard the old ones, take new ones, purify the other furnishings as prescribed, sacrifice with the earth sacrifice, and then dwell there; for by the <s>vāstusavana</s> there is purification of household things. The <s>āghāra</s> belongs to the <s>vāstusavana</s>. He should sacrifice with the two verses, '<s>Vāstoṣpati</s>, acknowledge us' and '<s>Vāstoṣpati</s>, be favorable.' 'Svāhā to the earth sacrifice' and 'svāhā to the sacrificial deity, to the sister' are two formulas whose deity is the earth sacrifice. 'The goddess <s>Medinī</s>, divine, gold-wombed, ocean-bearing, Sāvitrī, on every peak, surrounded by wind, lying in the waters' are five formulas whose deity is the earth. Having offered the <s>vyāhṛtis</s>, he proclaims the auspicious day. Saying 'O <s>Agni</s>, I take the fire,' he takes fire from the fire-place with a bundle of darbha grass. Beginning from the first, the Aindra <s>bhuvaṃga</s>, or from the base of the dwelling wall, outside and inside, he should go around to the left from the <s>brahmasthāna</s> and have the fire carried around, then send it out by the western door. In the same way, with 'Smaller than the small,' he should let water stream after it from a vessel, and with what remains he sprinkles everywhere. Thus there should be the fire-circuit and the water-stream, beginning either from the Vāruṇa, Yāmya, or Saumya <s>bhuvaṃga</s>.

children.text: ye te śataṃ varuṇoduttamamayāś cāgna āpaḥ sṛjantu snigdhānīti catvāro varuṇadaivatyā viśve devasya viśve adyeti dvau vaiśvadevāvato devā idaṃ viṣṇus trīṇi padā viṣṇoḥ karmāṇi tadviṣṇoḥ paramaṃ tad viprāsa iti ṣaḍvaiṣṇavā dvāvādyāvityeke rudramanyaṃ tryambakamiti dvau rudradaivatyau brahma jajñānaṃ hiraṇyagarbha iti dvau brahmadaivatyau miśravāsasa etān ghnataitāniti dvau kauberau yuvam etānyagnīṣomāvānyaṃ diva iti trayo 'gnīṣomīyā bṛhaspatirdevānāṃ bṛhaspatiḥ somaṃ bṛhaspate ati yadupayāmagṛhīta iti catvāro bārhaspatyāḥ trātāramindraṃ mahām indro ya ojasā mahām indro nṛvad bhuvas tvam indrenda sānasiṃ pra sasāhiṣe 'smākamindro bhūtasyendro dyaurindraṃ praṇavantam indro vṛtramindro babhūvendro 'smāniti trayodaśaindrāḥ yamo dādhāra namaste nirṛtaya iti dvau yāmyau mitrasya carṣaṇīdhṛto mitro janān pra sa mitreti trayo maitrāḥ bhūmiyajñadaivatyādayo vyāhṛtyantā ijyante tasmād dvyuttaraṃ śatamāhutayo vāstusavanasyāntahomamiti vijñāyate ||
children.translated_text: The four verses addressed to <s>Varuṇa</s>, beginning “Those hundred of yours,” “By <s>Varuṇa</s>,” “Most excellent,” and “And, O <s>Agni</s>, may the waters release the unctuous ones”; the two <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> verses beginning “Of every god” and “All today”; the six Vaiṣṇava verses beginning “Then, O gods,” “This <s>Viṣṇu</s>,” “The three steps,” “The deeds of <s>Viṣṇu</s>,” “That highest place of <s>Viṣṇu</s>,” and “That the inspired ones”; or, according to some, the first two only; the two verses addressed to <s>Rudra</s>, “Another <s>Rudra</s>” and “Tryambaka”; the two addressed to <s>Brahman</s>, “<s>Brahman</s> was born” and “<s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>”; the two <s>Kaubera</s> verses, “Clothed in mixed garments” and “Strike these, these”; the three addressed to <s>Agni</s> and <s>Soma</s>, “You two, these,” “O <s>Agnīṣomau</s>,” and “Another from heaven”; the four <s>Bārhaspatya</s> verses, “<s>Bṛhaspati</s> of the gods,” “<s>Bṛhaspati</s>,” “<s>Soma</s>,” and “O <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, when what is taken in the upayāma”; the thirteen Indra verses, “<s>Indra</s> the protector,” “The great <s>Indra</s>,” “<s>Indra</s> who by strength,” “Great <s>Indra</s>,” “You become like men,” “You, O <s>Indra</s>,” “O <s>Indra</s>, you win,” “You mightily overcome,” “Our <s>Indra</s>,” “<s>Indra</s> of what has come to be,” “Heaven is <s>Indra</s>,” “They praise <s>Indra</s>,” “<s>Indra</s> smote <s>Vṛtra</s>,” “<s>Indra</s> became,” and “<s>Indra</s> for us” [the transmitted count is irregular]; the two Yama verses, “<s>Yama</s> upheld” and “Homage to <s>Nirṛti</s>”; the three Maitra verses, “Of <s>Mitra</s>, who upholds men,” “<s>Mitra</s> the people,” and “Forward, O <s>Mitra</s>”; and the offerings beginning with those whose deity is the earth-sacrifice and ending with the <s>vyāhṛtis</s> are sacrificed. Therefore the inner oblation of the vāstusavana is understood to consist of one hundred and two oblations.

children.text: atha daśame dvādaśe vāhni bhavatyutthānaṃ tathaiva jātakāgniṃ samāropya yāvantyasya karmāṇi tāni sarvāṇi mathitvāsminneva kuryādvisṛjya laukikāgnāvityeke snātvāgāraṃ yathoktaṃ śodhayet kṣurakarmādinā śuddho bhūmiyajñamasagotreṇa yājayedityeke tathā haraṇamaupāsanasya dhātādi pañca vāruṇaṃ mūlahomo bhojanaṃ brāhmaṇānām ||
children.translated_text: Then, on the tenth or twelfth day, there is the rising. In the same way, having transferred the birth-fire, he should churn out all the fires required for whatever rites are his and perform all those rites in that very fire; according to some, after dismissing it, they are done in an ordinary fire. Having bathed, he should purify the house as prescribed. Having been purified by shaving and the other acts, he should have the earth-sacrifice performed by someone not of the same <s>gotra</s>, according to some. Likewise there is the removal of the <s>aupāsana</s> fire, the five oblations beginning with <s>Dhātṛ</s>, the five Vāruṇa oblations, the root oblation, and the feeding of Brāhmaṇas.

children.text: atha nāmakaraṇam ā catvāriṃśaddivasād ā pañcāśaddinādvā pāke naināṃ niyuñjīta tatraiva śubhe puṃnāmni nakṣatre paristīryāgniṃ tathāsīnasyākṣataṃ kumārasya mūrdhni vinyasya pañca vāruṇaṃ prājāpatyaṃ sviṣṭākāraṃ ca hutvāsya pūrvavattrivṛtprāśanaṃ dīrghāntam abhiniṣṭhāntaṃ vā ghoṣavadādyantaraṃ dvipratiṣṭhitāntasthaṃ mṛṣṭākṣarapadasvaraṃ dvivarṇaṃ caturvarṇaṃ vā nāma śasyate yathoktaṃ mama nāma prathamamiti gotranāmayuktaṃ tadarhaṃ nāma kuryāt dve nāmanī tu nakṣatranāma rahasyam agnyādhānāt paramāhitāgnyādisvakarmāntaṃ prakāśaṃ nāma bhaved akṣatodakapuṣpānnarasagandhasamaiḥ pāṇibhyāṃ dakṣiṇetarābhyāṃ kumārasya śāṃkarir iveti kanyāyā nandevānandadāyinīti vadanpādata ārabhya krameṇa dehāṅgasaṃdhau śirasi ca nikṣipetpuṇyāham ||
children.translated_text: Now the name-giving. Up to the fortieth day, or up to the fiftieth day, he should not employ her in cooked-food rites. There itself, under an auspicious lunar mansion bearing a male name, he spreads the grass around the fire. When he is seated thus, he places unbroken rice on the boy's head and offers the five Vāruṇa oblations, the Prājāpatya oblation, and the <s>sviṣṭākāra</s>. Then, as before, he has him eat the threefold mixture. A name is recommended that ends in a long vowel or in <s>abhinisṭhāna</s>, that has a voiced sound at beginning and end, that has a semi-vowel set between two consonants, that has clean syllables, word, and accent, and that consists of two or four syllables. As prescribed, with “My name first,” he should make for him a suitable name joined with the <s>gotra</s>-name. There are two names: the lunar-mansion name is secret until the establishment of the sacred fire and through the personal rites beginning with consecration of the sacred fires, while the public name is for open use. With unbroken rice, water, flowers, food, juices, and perfumes in both hands, right and left, he should place them on the boy, saying “like <s>Śāṃkari</s>,” and on a girl, saying “O rejoicing one, giver of joy”; beginning from the feet, he deposits them in order on the joints of the bodily limbs and on the head. Then there is the proclamation of the auspicious day.

children.text: atha varṣavardhanaṃ dārakasya janmanakṣatraṃ yaddaivatyaṃ sāsya devatā pradhānā bhavati tasmādāghāraṃ hutvā tadadhidevatā nakṣatrāṇi ca juhuyādagnaye kṛttikābhyaḥ prajāpataye rohiṇyai somāya mṛgaśīrṣāya rudrāyārdrāyā adityai punarvasūbhyāṃ bṛhaspataye tiṣyāya sarpebhya āśreṣābhyaḥ pitṛbhyo maghābhyo 'ryamṇe phalgunībhyāṃ bhagāya phalgunībhyāṃ savitre hastāya tvaṣṭre citrāyai vāyave niṣṭyāyā indrāgnibhyāṃ viśākhābhyāṃ mitrāyānūrādhebhya indrāya jyeṣṭhāyai prajāpataye mūlāyādbhyo 'ṣāḍhābhyo viśvebhyo devebhyo 'ṣāḍhābhyo brahmaṇe 'bhijite viṣṇave śroṇāyai vasubhyaḥ śraviṣṭhābhyo varuṇāya śatabhiṣaje 'jāyaikapade proṣṭhapadebhyo 'haye budhniyāya proṣṭhapadebhyaḥ pūṣṇe revatyā aśvibhyām aśvayugbhyāṃ yamāyāpabharaṇībhyaḥ svāheti vyāhṛtiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Now the annual increase rite. Whatever deity presides over the boy's birth lunar mansion becomes his principal deity. Therefore, after offering the <s>āghāra</s>, he should offer to that presiding deity and to the lunar mansions: to <s>Agni</s> for the <s>Kṛttikās</s>; to <s>Prajāpati</s> for <s>Rohiṇī</s>; to <s>Soma</s> for <s>Mṛgaśīrṣa</s>; to <s>Rudra</s> for <s>Ārdrā</s>; to <s>Aditi</s> for the <s>Punarvasūs</s>; to <s>Bṛhaspati</s> for <s>Tiṣya</s>; to the Serpents for the <s>Āśreṣās</s>; to the Ancestors for the <s>Maghās</s>; to <s>Aryaman</s> for the <s>Phalgunīs</s>; to <s>Bhaga</s> for the <s>Phalgunīs</s>; to <s>Savitṛ</s> for <s>Hasta</s>; to <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s> for <s>Citrā</s>; to <s>Vāyu</s> for <s>Niṣṭyā</s>; to <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s> for the <s>Viśākhās</s>; to <s>Mitra</s> for the <s>Anurādhās</s>; to <s>Indra</s> for <s>Jyeṣṭhā</s>; to <s>Prajāpati</s> for <s>Mūla</s>; to the Waters for the <s>Āṣāḍhās</s>; to all the gods for the <s>Āṣāḍhās</s>; to <s>Brahman</s> for <s>Abhijit</s>; to <s>Viṣṇu</s> for <s>Śroṇā</s>; to the <s>Vasus</s> for the <s>Śraviṣṭhās</s>; to <s>Varuṇa</s> for <s>Śatabhiṣaj</s>; to <s>Aja Ekapad</s> for the <s>Proṣṭhapadas</s>; to <s>Ahir Budhnya</s> for the <s>Proṣṭhapadas</s>; to <s>Pūṣan</s> for <s>Revatī</s>; to the <s>Aśvins</s> for the <s>Aśvayujes</s>; and to <s>Yama</s> for the <s>Apabharaṇīs</s>, each with “svāhā.” Then he offers the <s>vyāhṛti</s>.

children.text: ṛṣabhaṃ vairavaṇam agnīṣomīyaṃ vaiṣṇavaṃ dhātādi mūlahomaṃ yaddevādi kūṣmāṇḍahomam ā sāvitravratabandhājjuhotyupanītasya ca tattadvratasūktāni vedasnātakasya yadahni vivāho bhavati māsike vārṣike cāhni tasminyatstriya āhuḥ pāraṃparyāgataṃ śiṣṭācāraṃ tattatkaroti tathāgniṣṭomādiyajñānām ādhānanakṣatre varṣānte karoti tadevaṃ vartamānasya yadyaṣṭamāsādhikāśītivarṣāṇi ravivarṣeṇādhigānyadhigaccheyuḥ sa dṛṣṭasahasracandro bhavati tamenaṃ kriyāyuktaṃ puṇyakṛttamaṃ brahmaśarīramityācakṣate tasmānnāndīmukhaṃ kṛtvā śuklapakṣe śuddhe 'hani pūrvāhṇe pūrvavaddhutvā tathaiva kapila iveti vṛddhasya vṛddhāyā vā vadannakṣatodakādīnmūrdhnyādadhyāt sarvadevatāḥ sahasraṃ ca brāhmaṇānāmarcanabalibhyāmannena tarpayet grāmaṃ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya sāyaṃ sthaṇḍile sahasraṃ piṣṭena somarūpāṇi karoti rājatena pātreṇa kumudapattraiḥ somasyārcanaṃ tasya dakṣiṇe rohiṇīgaṇaṃ vāme cānāvṛṣṭigaṇamarcayati sahasraśaḥ suvarṇarajatamuktādīni śaktyā vastrataṇḍulāpūpāni ca dadyādaśvamedhaphalāvāptyai varṣavardhanamiti vijñāyate ||
children.translated_text: He offers the <s>ṛṣabha</s>, the <s>Vairavaṇa</s>, the <s>Agnīṣomīya</s>, the Vaiṣṇava rite, the basic oblation beginning with <s>Dhātṛ</s>, and the <s>Kūṣmāṇḍa</s> oblation beginning <s>yad deva</s>, up to the binding of the <s>Sāvitrī</s> vow; and, for one who has been initiated, the respective vow-hymns. For one who has completed Vedic study, on the day on which his marriage takes place, and on the monthly and yearly days, he performs whatever women call the inherited custom that has come down by tradition and is the conduct of the learned. Likewise, in the case of sacrifices beginning with the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>, he performs them at the lunar mansion of the establishment of the fires, at the end of the year. One who lives in this way, if eighty years plus eight months measured by the solar year have been reached, is one who has seen a thousand moons. Such a man, joined with the rites, the best of meritorious men, is called a body of <s>Brahman</s>. Therefore, after performing the <s>nāndīmukha</s> rite, in the bright fortnight, on a pure day, in the forenoon, he offers oblations as before. In the same way, saying <s>kapila iva</s>, for an old man or an old woman he should place unbroken rice, water, and the rest on the head. He should satisfy all the deities and a thousand Brahmins with worship, bali offerings, and food. Having gone clockwise around the village, in the evening, on a prepared altar, he makes a thousand lunar forms from flour. With a silver vessel and white-lotus leaves he worships <s>Soma</s>; to his right he worships the <s>Rohiṇī</s> group, and to his left the <s>Anāvṛṣṭi</s> group. According to his means he should give gold, silver, pearls, and the like by the thousand, and also garments, rice, and cakes. It is understood as the rite increasing years, for the attainment of the fruit of the <s>Aśvamedha</s>.

children.text: atha ṣaṣṭhe māsyannaprāśanaṃ śuklapakṣe dine śuddhe tatrājyenāghāro dhātādi mūlahomaṃ pūrvavattrivṛtprāśanaṃ prāṅmukhaṃ maṅgalayuktaṃ kumāraṃ viṣṭaramāropya bhūr apām iti pāyasam annaṃ prāśayedyoge yoge tavastaram ityācamanaṃ dadātyatha pravāsāgamanaṃ puṣpāpūpadakṣiṇādisambhārān kumāraṃ ca gṛhītvā kanikradādim ālayaṃ guhasya gacchetpradakṣiṇamarcanaṃ praṇāmo guhasya tacchiṣṭena puṣpādinā guhasya śeṣamiti tannāmohitvā bālam alaṃkṛtya śāntiṃ vācayitvā nivartayetprokṣyāgataṃ somasya tvetyaṅgamāropyāyuṣe varcasa iti pitā mūrdhni jighrati vṛṣabhaṃ namaskṛtya dakṣiṇapāṇeḥ sāṅguṣṭhamaṅgulīr gṛhītvā kaniṣṭhādyagnirāyuṣmānityādikair visarjanam āyuṣṭe viśvataḥ pratiṣṭha vāyāviti dakṣiṇādikarṇayor japanamudaṅmukhaṃ brahmādidevānāṃ gurūṇāṃ ca praṇāmaṃ kārayet pādodakaṃ dattvā pūrvavat saguḍabhakṣyasyānnasya sapiṇḍaiḥ śrotriyaiḥ saha bhojanaṃ svastivācanaṃ piṇḍavardhanamiti vijñāyate ||
children.translated_text: Now, in the sixth month, the first feeding of solid food is performed. In the bright fortnight, on a pure day, there is an <s>āghāra</s> with clarified butter, the basic oblation beginning with <s>Dhātṛ</s>, and, as before, the threefold eating. Having placed the boy, facing east and adorned with auspicious things, on a seat, he should feed him milk-rice as food with <s>bhūr apām</s>. With <s>yoge yoge tavastaram</s> he gives water for sipping. Then, for return after travel, taking flowers, cakes, gifts, and other materials, and the boy as well, he should go to the temple of <s>Guha</s> with the verse beginning <s>kanikradat</s>. There are clockwise circumambulation, worship, and bowing to <s>Guha</s>. With the remainder belonging to <s>Guha</s>, namely flowers and the like, and saying that it is <s>Guha</s>’s remainder, he adorns the child, has the peace blessing recited, and brings him back. Having sprinkled the returned child, he places him on his lap with <s>somasya tvā</s>, and with <s>āyuṣe varcasaḥ</s> the father smells his head. After bowing to <s>Vṛṣabha</s>, he takes the fingers of the right hand together with the thumb, and, beginning from the little finger, performs the dismissal with formulas beginning <s>agnir āyuṣmān</s>. With <s>āyuṣ te viśvataḥ pratiṣṭha vāyau</s> he murmurs into the right and other ears. Facing north, he should make the child bow to the gods beginning with <s>Brahmā</s> and to the teachers. Having given foot-water, as before, there is a meal of food with sweet molasses together with <s>sapiṇḍas</s> and learned <s>śrotriyas</s>, an auspicious proclamation, and the rite increasing the body; so it is understood.

children.text: atha varṣe prathame tṛtīye vā cauḍakam uttarāyaṇe pakṣa āpūryamāṇe puṃnāmnyāghāro mūlahomānte maṅgalayuktam agner aparasyāṃ kumāram upaveśyottare sākṣataṃ gośakṛccharāve gṛhītvā mātā brahmacārī vā dhārayecchivo nāmāsīti grahaṇaṃ kṣurasya śivā no bhavatheti śilāyāṃ tīkṣṇīkaraṇaṃ godānam unaktviti gavādidakṣiṇākaraṇam āpa undantvity apāṃ sekaṃ śirasyoṣadhe trāyasvainamiti sākṣatāṅkuradarbhau prāguttarāgrau mastake sthāpayetsvadhite mainam hiṃsīriti kṣuraṃ nidhāyordhvāgram oṣadhīriti yenāvapaditi yena pūṣetyasāvāyuṣeti pūrvādipradakṣiṇaṃ darbhaṃ saromāṇaṃ chittvā jyok ca sūryaṃ dṛśa iti cūḍāṃ vibhajedṛṣikrameṇa svasyaikārṣadvyārṣatryārṣapañcārṣasaptārṣāc cūḍā vibhajed anuditasyaikāmidam aham amuṣyetyudumbaradarbhayor mūle goṣṭhe vācchādayet snātaṃ vastrādinālaṃkṛtyopaveśya dakṣiṇe pañca prāyaścittādi dhātādi pañca vāruṇaṃ mūlahomaṃ hutvā puṇyāhaṃ kṛtvā nāpitāyānnadānaṃ gavādidakṣiṇāṃ gurave surāṇāṃ pūjanaṃ tarpaṇaṃ brāhmaṇānāmannena karotītyaṣṭādaśa saṃskārāḥ śārīrāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Now, in the first year or in the third, the <s>cauḍaka</s> tonsure is performed, during the northern course of the sun, in the waxing fortnight, under a lunar mansion with a male name. After the <s>āghāra</s> and at the end of the basic oblation, he seats the boy, adorned with auspicious things, west of the fire. To the north, the mother or a celibate student should hold a dish of cow dung mixed with unbroken rice. With <s>śivo nāmāsi</s> there is the taking of the razor; with <s>śivā no bhavatha</s>, sharpening it on a stone; with <s>godānam unaktu</s>, the giving of cows and other gifts; with <s>āpa undantu</s>, sprinkling with water. Saying <s>oṣadhe trāyasvainam</s>, he places on the head unbroken rice, a sprout, and two blades of darbha with their tips toward the northeast. With <s>svadhite mainam hiṃsīḥ</s> he sets down the razor. With <s>ūrdhvāgram oṣadhīḥ</s>, <s>yenāvapat</s>, <s>yena pūṣā</s>, and <s>asāv āyuṣā</s>, proceeding clockwise from the east and the other directions, he cuts the darbha together with hair, and with <s>jyok ca sūryaṃ dṛśe</s> he divides the topknot. According to the sequence of the seers, he should divide the topknot of his own line, whether one-seer, two-seer, three-seer, five-seer, or seven-seer; for one whose lineage is not recited, he divides a single topknot. With <s>idam aham amuṣya</s>, he should conceal the cut hair at the root of an udumbara tree and darbha grass, or in a cow-pen. Having bathed him, adorned him with garments and the like, and seated him, he offers on the southern side the five oblations beginning with expiation, the five beginning with <s>Dhātṛ</s>, the five Vāruṇa oblations, and the basic oblation. Having performed the auspicious-day rite, he gives food to the barber, gives cows and other gifts to the teacher, and performs worship of the gods and satisfaction of the Brahmins with food. These are the eighteen bodily <s>saṃskāras</s>.
